REVIEW MADE IN 2015 OPINIONS MAY VARY
Do you want the honest opinion about Assassin's creed Unity from a diehard fan of the AC franchise? Well, sit back, cause this is gonna be one hell of a ride.
Lets talk about the hype... When Unity was annonced back in summer of 2014 i was excited. "an AC game whitout any stupid ship gameplay? ill love it :D" and then it begun. Me and the rest of the community started hyping up the game and thats a bad thing since the game developers has trouble delivering and we shouldent expect this much from ubisoft anyway. So the hype basically destroyed unity... but more on that later, lets talk about the game.
Story
Assassin's creed Unity takes place druing the french revulution. In the present, the modern assassins are racing against the Templars to find, shortend down, a soon-to-be animus test subject with a extra amount of memories about his ancestors. If the templars find him first, they will be able to locate a large amount of information about " the first civilization" and find more pieces of eden. The assassin's ofcourse wont let this happen and decides to send multiple assassins into the animuses in order to find information about the soon-to-be test subject before the templars can. We take control of a nameless/faceless Assassins that inturn takes controll of the soon-to-be Assassins Arno Dorian. We follow Arno from a child, to a young adult and finally a full grown Adult, where the assassin part kicks of. whitout spoiling anything, Arno eventully runs into the test subjects ancestor and proceds to find him in the present time.
But thats just the icing of the cake, theres a lot more going on in paris with tones of side quests witch mixes in a bunch of famous and historical characters that Arno helps out in various ways.
Graphics
As a next gen title the game looks pretty..that means if you actully manage to play on anything over medium quality.. Thats the real problem with Unity, its choppy framerate. Even though i might suffer from the occasionally freeze of fps drop when i enter a new area or a new quest loads up, it docent even come close to what ive seen some people, with far better computers than i have, run into. Some people cant even play the game on low quality, and cutscenes cant even be watched for some of them. Lets go over what we know.
Im fully capable of playing the game on high quality, but i stick to medium since i dont really care about the graphics. Like i mentioned before, the cutscenes run smoothly and nice for me and rare frame drops and freezes happen occasionally but my computer is kinda slow, so its expected. overall, it runs smoothly for me and i dont have any major problems.
JESUS CHRIST! Some people cant even play the game because of the constant drops in frame rate, freezes and overall  choppyness. Turning around barely renders and actions takes point to registrer.
Yeah, its that bad!! I used to consider my self lucky that i my game only freezed about 3 times per session, but now i think that my game is some kind of god sent gift considering some people crash, freeze or drop 50 frames per minute!!
The pc realese has recived multiple optimizations but i cant tell the diffrence, i hope ubisoft decides to fix the graphics at some point.
Gameplay
Actully, this is the games strong point. There are many sidequests and constant events in the streets around paris, multiple chests that can be approached diffrently and collectibles spread throughout the city, ready to be collected!!  So you definitely wont be bored while your roaming the city. Unity also decides to step back to the days of AC Revulations by having alot of weapons, armors and skills! You can earn money but investing in buldings, loot it or steal it. The parkour system has also been simplified, as you can control your way through the city much easier. By holding down the UP button while free-running, Arno will jump higher of climb buildings faster, and by holding the DOWN button, Arno will decend buildings more quickly, jump downwards while freeruning on buildings or more quickly move past small obstacels. If neither of these arnt your cup of tea, you can simply hold down the sprint button and Arno will perform either UP or DOWN as he see fits. Although this makes free running look cooler and easier to perform, its kind of unnecessary. You will also recive money from quests and community events. Thankfully there isent a "level" requirement to buy or equip the weapons, you simply have to buy them and equip them. Unity also introduces the phantom blade, witch replaces the knife, hidden gun and crossbow. it has its own small arrows and berserker darts, witch makes a return in this game. Unity also has diffrent classes that you can play in order to findout witch playstyle fits you the most.
Combat- More challenging than in other AC games, in this one you cant just counter and kill everybody in a giant chain, as you actually need skill and you need to be on the lookout for heavy swingers and marksman that can interrupt your combos. This playstyle is simple in the beginning but picks up in difficulty later in the game.
Stealth- Yeah, this game actully gives out Assassin a chance to hide. You can crouch behind object and hide behind corners. Sneak around, distreacting targets to sneak past them and lockpicking doors. This playstyle is more difficult to master, since you always have to be alert and your rear and minimap and make effective use of the eagle sense. You can thow smoke bombs and cherry bombs to make distractions to either assassinate a target or sneak past them. Using the phantom blade's effectively takes practise and you always have to have a plan B, in case you get discovered.
Marksman/Sniper- Definitely the easiest class to master, the Marksman/Sniper favours Guns and the phantom blade over pure combat strength. This class is all about staying out of combat and being support for other Assassins, however if you play by yourself, this class can be quite tricky to main, since you need to stay out of sight more often.
So with some selection in the mix, this game surely mixes it up, however, this classes are simply subclasses, and they all go through the same quests and story. no diffrence. You may have noticed how i mentioned " however if you play by your self" before. Thats because Unity has the heaviest emphasis on Co-op than any other AC unity game. You nee to join a club in order to 100% the game, certian, bigger, harder missions require help from other assassins, witch can become annoying after a while, thankfully, there is still the singel player story HOWEVER, its incredibly short. So if your planning to get this game, make sure you have some freinds to play with, otherwise you might sit there and not be able to finish certain missons.
CONCLUSSION
So its obvious that i like the game, but can i recommend this to you? or can i recommend this to someone who has never played an AC game before?... well short and simple... No. I wouldent be able to reccomend this game to, well, anyone and still feel good about my self. This game, although it looks good, for some lucky people, and plays good, if you like constanly getting pepered about club compition and boosts, it still falls short compered to other games. Although ive always liked AC and gladly thrown my money at them, they really disappointed me with Unity. The lacking story, the cliche ending, the AI isent very good, the lacking single player story and MICROTRANSACTIONS?! No. dont buy this peice of money grab. and dont make this your first AC game, buy AC2 in that case. But, if i cant convince you, please approch this game with cation.... This is certainly the last game i preorder from Ubisoft. And dont trust Uplay. As of today, im not gonna recommend this to my freinds. As a hardcore fan of AC, this game fell down under the hype and just became a short, money grabbing side project..
And remember guys, Udontplay. Ubisoft plays YOU. And thanks for reading.

Dialogue options have enough variety if you're trying to follow the story. Your options are limited in a way that you can't derail the plot so someone looking to test the limits or has too high expectations of freedom may become frustrated. My take on it is that it offers a good story as a backbone and your choices just help flesh out the details.
The dialogue timer often forces you have to pick based on instinct. I found it nice because not only was I engaged with the story, I had to chose what I would do in real time (instead of metagame it). I still used the rewind function several times but I recommend doing your first playthrough blind and choosing options that match what you would do.
If english isn't your first language (or your reading and/or comprehension speed isn't fast enough) then you will have trouble on the faster timers. In the fast ones I was able to get through by skimming the responses, making a gut choice, and then reacting before the time ran out. However I do think there should be a casual mode that extends timers to accomodate for people who can't/are unwilling to make choices on the spot. (Edit: WD2's space bar to pause was a better solution than a casual mode)
I'd recommend to anyone looking for a good thriller/drama/horror story experience.

SPECS: AMD FX-8300, Nvidia GeForce GTX 760 (2GB VRAM), 8 GB RAM, Windows 10, 10 MBit/sec download speed
GRAPHICS: Beautiful.  Absolutely beautiful.  My rig runs this game 60 fps at most times with all settings on High, only slowing down to 30 fps during cutscenes or timeouts.  I've experienced a crash every once in a blue moon, but that's to be expected from a game that just got released.  Other than that, no problems at all with running this game.
CONTROLS: Listen, all the people complaining about not being able to change keyboard controls are correct, but you should NOT be playing this game with a keyboard.  Even if you could customize the layout, it would be a terrible experience.  Get a controller or don't get this game.
MYCAREER: Yes, the Spike Lee career is a bit cheesy at times dialouge-wise, but the problems that everyone seems to be complaining about didn't influence my experience with the mode.  I made a white MyPlayer, and sure, it looked a bit weird with my twin sister and family being black, but after the first cutscene I just completely forgot about it.  The beginning part of the mode is solid, and the college experience was very fun.  However, my major gripe with MyCareer is how low of a rating you start out with and how hard it is to improve from that.  You go from dominating the high school/college game to getting 4 pts a game in the NBA if you're lucky.  Once you start leveling up your player, the mode is insanely fun.
MYGM: Very much like 2K15's mode, except with Team Relocation and slightly more control over your team.  If you liked it last year, you'll enjoy it this year.
MYPLAYER: Creating your player is almost exactly the same, still no Face Scan.
MYTEAM: Once again, just like last years as far as I can tell, but you can customize your court, branding, and uniforms once you get far enough into the mode.
COURT DESIGN: Insanely addicting, spent over an hour creating my team designs for Pro-Am and will probably do the same for MyTeam and if I relocate the Bucks in MyGM.  Very customizable, can pretty much do whatever you want.
ONLINE: I played one online game just to test the mode and I experienced absolutely no slowdown.  None whatsoever.  It's amazing and I love it.  In fact, I haven't had any online problems with this game AT ALL, except for a day or two when 2KTV was unaccessible (but who cares about that anyway?).  Good job on 2K's part for nailing the servers this year.
CONCLUSION: An excellent game with improvement in nearly every aspect, a few crashes but no graphical glitches or problems to be seen.  All basketball fans should pick this game up.
RATING: 9.5/10

There are many improvements  and changes in NBA 2k16 that make this game feel like a different game than NBA 2k15.
I started out with NBA 2k15 and straight away I could feel that the game was one of the best sport sims I had ever played.
NBA 2k16 pickup where NBA 2k15 left off by tuning the game even more. Setting a screen is no longer just run to spot and press the button. If you are moving and setting a screen you will cause a foul resulting in a turnover. Blocking seems more genuine. I caught my self yelling out NICE!! when the AI denied a dunk. The animations are really awesome.
The commentary is another thing that really makes the 2k games so good. They really build up the whole sports feeling and I love it. It's really great.
But this release is not without flaws. You all have probably already read about MyCareer mode which isn't the story that everyone expected. I won't go into details but what you should know is that you are not playing YOUR future. You are playing an ongoing MOVIE and you have no impact on the story at all. The Spike Lee "experience" is just that, a movie and probably not what was expected. In that aspect nba 2k15 was light years better because you want options and different outcomes depending on the choices you make and reactions to what's really happening on the floor. Nba 2k16 is not that but it doesn't make this a great game.
A second flaw are the bugs. There are just simply too many to be called a full release. Penalty shot, the camera pov starts to shake like there is an earthquake.. I'm guessing this is not intentionally as it's horrible when it happens (which is quite often). Fouls are called by the commentary but no fouls are given in game.  The list can be made long with bugs that will need to be fixed and probably are going to be soo to.
The conclusion is that you are not paying for a full game at this stage. You are paying full price for a game in beta stage. There is no way around it. However, the game is really good. You can feel it through the bugs and glitches and once it's been tuned it will be one of the best games out there.  So I'm going to give this game 2 ratings.

NBA 2k16 is even more realistic than 2k15 and that is why although the game has some serious flaws as of right now, the potential and what it will be is simply too good not to get.

I just couldn't wait and even though the bugs I'll keep playing nba 2k16 even though I'm still having fun with NBA 2k15 as the AI and the game mechanism behind 2k16 are just that much better.

Lords of the Fallen is one of those games that are very underrated because it is too close to the original ones from where the devs took their inspiration to create this, and people tend to label those games just as a bad copy, a bad version of the original game. Which is the case most of the times, but not with Lords of the Fallen.
First of all, there are some very clear differences between this game and the Souls series. Lords of the Fallen is more focused on its story and how to present it to the player than the Souls  games that are more focused on the world, difficulty, and how to beat the adversaries and situations, kind of leaving the details of the story "hidden". That is something that I enjoyed very much, because I am a player more of roleplay, story and exploration of the world and its characters than a fan of hack and slash. So I am more concerned of being part of that world than to conquer it. If you favour those things as well you are probably going to enjoy this game. It is not that the Souls series don't have good stories, far from that, but the story, the details, except for the main part, it is too "concealed". Take the complains about Lords of the Fallen: Most of them are about how bad people consider the combat to be. I disagree it is bad but I agree with the fact that there aren't many options..
Second, everybody says that the Souls games are hard. I don't think this way. Perhaps because I am of a time when you had to go back all the way to the start of the game if you fail to beat it and that rarely happens nowadays. I think the Souls games demand time, patience, and practice, but it is not very much a matter of skill, except perhaps when facing another player, and that's where Lords of the Fallen stays far behind the original games, not having multiplayer options. But at least you won't explode in anger because you played 20 hours only to get an item from a Dual Skeleton Katana Dark Phantom or because no matter what you can't beat that part and you need to farm (and farm, and farm and keep farming) and improve before continuing the game. Without resorting to duplicating itens. Meaning: Lords of the Fallen  won't be a pain in the ♥♥♥♥♥ to solve something like any Souls games.
Lords of the Fallen is considerable easier than any Souls game, but it does have an unbalanced difficulty: Everything is easy, except for the Worshipper boss and one or other situation. Plus the difficulty changes a lot depending on the class that you choose.
Third the graphics and the concepts of the world: The Souls series have a nice concept that I prefer very much over the Lords of the Fallen. Both games are based on fantasy worlds, but the concepts for the Souls were more "realist" and dark, to stimulate and translate the atmosphere of the worlds of those games, this is true both to Demon Soul as well as to all of the Dark Souls and even to Bloodborne, while the concepts for the Lords of the Fallen are more exaggerated, sometimes even disproportional, everything is too huge, armors are huge, weapons are huge, the atmosphere is more colorful, etc.  Even the rules for carrying weight (for the inventory), don't really make much sense in this game. The weight of what you wear, of what is equipped, is counting, but the weight of any item that you carry in your inventory is completely ignored, so you can carry ten thousand weapons. But the way the character moves (and the creatures as well) are very nice, small movements are very fluid, people complain a lot about the speed of this game but it works for me; Harkyn does have his troubles dealing with heavy weapons, sometimes he can't even lift them unless you choose the two hands option. But he tries to lift them and fails. It is a nice touch. So, it is really nothing that bothers, after all it is just a game and that doesn't ruin the "immersion".
One thing that kind of ruins the immersion, though, is the graphic. The graphic of Lords of The Fallen is very nice, all the details, the atmosphere, the character and creature designs, the landscapes, the change of tones and scenarios much more varied than on the Souls series... all of this are nice. The problem is that there are too many graphic issues. Dead enemies or broken props sometimes stays floating in the air. That bothers a little, but it is no big deal. The camera sometimes may be a problem too.
The game has some other minor bugs and mistakes, sometimes you trespass an enemy instead of hitting it or vice versa, your skills are resetted and the game changes your class automatically (that actually only happened twice with me), some crashes, etc. But they are no big deal as well.
So, all of the problems of the game are not really big issues, and despite being labeled as a copy, the good points are much more and far better than the bad points. In general, the atmosphere, graphics (when free of bugs), music and sound and especially and most important the rhythm of the game are all great.
Final Considerations:
If you don't know or if you are not an avid fan of any Demon or Dark Souls, you may like this game, despite the fact that it was inspired on those other games. Actually you are probably going to enjoy it even more because you won't be comparing all the time.
The story is ok, the characters doesn't appear very much but they have some nice interactions, dialogues (simple but they work to show the world of the game and its story) and the most important thing about this game: it is very fun to play. You can play for many hours and forget the time.

"Do you recommend this game" No. Not really at all. (TL;DR down the bottom)
(You'll notice that I haven't completed the game on my account. I have, however, on the PS version at a friend's house.)
TT's engine isn't great. It's not bug-free: I've had to restart the level due to glitches such as characters not being usable when they shouldn't, jumping through walls, and the Special Ablities being glitchy.
The openable caves - which is a fairly good idea - aren't great. They're often really hard. Not hard as in challenging: hard as in boring. I'll take a cave near the Misty Mountains, where you have to jump on spiky platforms which spikes pop up periodically.
The problem with this is that failing takes FAR TOO LONG: you have to go AROUND, then up, then back on the platform... *yawn* It'd be easier if they just killed you at the bottom.
Then there's a set of three spiky platforms in a row. There's no way you can get past this that I've found. Running spends to long, jumping is useless, and as far as I know no character has a speed boost. (Feel free to correct me on this)
Now, I'll go to the bosses. They're far, far better than Lego LoTR (in which EVERY boss has EXACTLY the same attacks), but they're not that great. There's often a key combination which you have to press. The problem is that you have to know the combination: the time it gives you isn't enough. So you have a pain in the rear and no mistake.
Co-op for these battles is horrible. There is literally NOTHING for the other character to do. Even when you have the sharpest sword of Middle Earth and you're against Azog, who has no armour, you can't hit him. No, the other character is raging at the time that they DON'T give for you to attack him.
This being said, a boss should not be beatable on the first try. One should have to THINK about it.
The problem is that this is taken the wrong way. They're only hittable at certain times: which I can understand, but the other times are simply just a pain.
The cutscenes are pretty good: if you don't like light humour then don't get this game.
Though, there's no clear way to skip them. Yes, it will come up with 'U' (Skip), but there's no way to control when it will do this. It is a slight nuisance that the Battle of the Five Armies is nonexistent and Erebore is marked by a Loot Dispenser - oh yes. That's the other thing I want to talk about.
Maybe my computer's something I dredged up from the seabed, but I meet the Reccommended Requirements, and even on lowst graphics settings the game still lags. There needs to be a setting: "Special Effects: Off/Low/High" That would save a lot of things.
So, about this loot. Given the lag, it's IMPOSSIBLE to mine anything as Bofur. I press the key immediately: right in the middle: and it keeps on going. I've had it mine perfectly thanks to the fact that it BOUNCED OFF THE END AND WENT BACK AGAIN.
Yes, my computer meets the Reccommended Requirements. The Reccommended ones.
Back to Loot again: Is there are USE for 1,000 rocks?
No?
Or 10,000 wood?
No?
At least you could sell it at the Dispenser.
Things are also completely unbalanced: Iron is often needed... but it's rarer than diamonds AND emerals, which are never needed except for getting that last Mithril Brick.
Loot is frankly pointless, and a waste of time. Just make things drop studs and ask the player to input 1,000 studs to unlock something or other... I'm not a dev.
Onto gameplay:
I can't stress how linear it is. You have 0 freedom.
I'll take as much of Riddles in the Dark as we were able to complete before it spazzes out (check my screenshots :P).
You have to knock down a skeleton to get a head to throw at something.
Hey... I have *checks* 100 rocks.
WHY CAN'T I JUST USE ONE OF THEM
Ok, so I'd need Dori to pull this down to get a Minikit... I have 50 rope. Can't I just use that?
You have a set number of things to do. No freedom. Do this, do this, and do that. Now, I'm not saying that TT should have coded that you could take out the trolls by pushing trees onto them and then attacking them in the face. I'm merely saying that there should be different options. You shouldn't have to go through the level with the game dictating what you can and cannot do.
Onto the Dwarves' ablities.
I have to say, TT did very well to give nearly all of them something useful.
Except for Thorin. He has nothing that he can do that somebody else cannot. Surely he, as the leader, should have the special stuff?
Onto actual gameplay: It's not great.
All the special stuff can only be used when the game tells you to. "Buddying up" is a complete waste of time and of patience if it isn't needed to complete the level. Pole Stacks are rather hard to control: you'd think that you'd jump off the pole, but no, you just climb up. Bombur's spring ability never comes out well. It's never used and when it IS, you're groaning that you're Player 2 and thus all the Dwarves are following Player 1, who is far, far away.
Ori's slingshot is similar. It's uselss for attacking (which I'll get to shortly) and is only used when it's needed. At least Dori's morningstar is effective in combat.
The attacking engine is horrible. By spamming out whatever key it is to attack, you won't get hurt unless it's a boss attack... and even then, that's unlikely. Anything ranged is USELESS. It's so much easier to walk up to the enemy and spam attacks rather than fuddle around with aiming something. Yes, it has an autotarget... but the autotarget seems to like aiming at the farthest away thing possible and not at the thing that is right in front of you hacking you down.
Speaking of attacking, the Necromancer boss.
PLEASE
This is the buggiest thing in the game.
You are a wizard (is far less exciting than it sounds: just like ranged units, but with the disatvantage of not being able to multi-fire and having a useless shield that protects against one attack in the GAME), and you have to shield yourself against the Necromancer's brick blasts. Easy, hey?
Except there's one orc that pops out and attacks you. No problem, right? It's just one. It's hardly an army.
Except that you as the player can scarcely attack him.  The default is to put the shield up. It's nigh on impossible to actually attack the orc. By the time you have, the Necromancer's launched another brick blast, and the orc is still hacking away at you.
Very, very, VERY fortunately, there's an area behind the tree on the left. The orc will never attack this space.
Onto the camera.
How can I put it nicely... It's like a wild horse on steroids. Very hard to control and rather unpredictable.
Oh, it works most of the time. Oh yes.
But the places where it doesn't work are often the places you need it the most. While exploring Middle-Earth you will be able to rotate it. You don't often need to, but it's helpful. However, this gets it to zoom in and out as it tries to get you a view of your character that isn't obscured by rock.
Levels... levels, now, are a different matter. The camera doesn't rotate.
It pans.
Meaning that it can be impossible to get a good view of what's happening. What I'd give for a nice top view where I can see where all those pesky platforms are... Why can't you just make it rotate? What is the PURPOSE of the pan?
Several people have bugged about the mouse controls. I'm not fussed about these. So what about the mouse? Do you not know how to use up/down and Enter on a keyboard on a main menu?
And... it even says it down the bottom! Oh yes! 'Up/Down' and 'Enter' (Select)!
TL;DR and finishing thoughts:
I've seen that the main reason people are reccomending this is basically because it's The Hobbit. This isn't a bad move: far from it. It's just that to me, the bugs and the pain over the engine make it unworthwhile.
If you're a Hobbit fan then you'll likely be enraged by the bugs in the engine.
They're not minor.

The main annoying trait is the "crafting" system. Which now requires you to have to correct elements of lego pieces collected throughout the levels to unlock various upgrades needed to gain other perks. Sadly I found this very tedious and added another layer of banality around it.
What the Lego Hobbit should have been was a single DLC expansion to the Lego LotR and contained within the same world. Sadly we got a large dull world, a dull cast and a thin, stretched out world. I've played this quite a lot.  It's a good pool game with problems. Mainly unreliable online play, frequent crashes (although not for everyone) and poor mouse controls.  I recommend using a controller.
I wrote this review in August.  Since then, nothing has changed.  It still has many annoying problems.  The developers don't provide any info on when things will be fixed or even if they're making any progess.  They didn't even seem aware of their own game's problems.
Multiplayer:
Finding a match is currently difficult.  There isn't a lobby to speak of.  Instead, you challenge another player and wait for them to accept or ignore.  There's a Quick Match option but I've never found a game this way. If you get into a game, it might play fine. More likely, you'll experience one of the many possible bugs or server issues. You can't mute mics.  There is no in-game chat.
Presentation:
The actual pool is very pretty.  The best I've seen.  The UI is not.  It could be improved a lot.
Audio:
Personally, I don't like the music but some people really do.  I turn it off.  The pool sounds are fine.  No complaints there.
Gameplay:
When it works, it plays great, for the most part.  Sometimes you can't see a shot as well as you would like but it's mostly fine.
There's a career mode which is just ok.  It's just a bunch of different game types against various AI.
The AI isn't great.  It pretends to be human so it can be slow.  It also can't do bank shots, doubles or plants.  It can get out of almost any snooker and doesn't play tactically at all.  It just makes amazing pots but it's very beatable most of the time.
You can play US 8-ball, 9-ball, UK 8-ball and a few others like killer and various potting/speed challenges.
So, it needs work.  If it was an early access game, I'd say it's a great alpha, a decent beta.  Released too early.
The devs don't say a lot so I'm just hoping they'll get this game up to a decent standard.

While the game mechanics itself are good, there are way too many negative aspects to this game to actually recommend it. In other reviews you can read all about the great graphics, nice music, good physics. However, most reviewers fail to name the negatives, of which there are plenty. Let me name just a few points which will frustrate you every time you encounter them.
-The menus are extremely wonky. It sometimes takes the game well over 5 seconds to do what you told it to do, which may be as simple as restarting a gamemode you just played. Sometimes the menus don't even work and you just keep pressing Enter without anything happening (this happens a lot when you attempt to enter a multiplayer game, the menu switches between "Quick Match" and the game mode selection screen).
-There is no fullscreen. If you try to play full screen the game crashes on start up. Using Alt + Enter you can get to fullscreen, but only up to 1280x720.
-You can't turn off the sound while ingame. You can turn down the sliders, but there will still be really soft sound in the background. To enable or disable sound you have to restart the game.
This game feels (and probably is) a very, very poor console port. The gameplay is solid and you will probably enjoy it, but the menus and especially the lack of full-screen is extremely frustrating. How they thought this was an acceptable product for sale is beyond me, because there are lots of probably easy to fix issues.

I've played a lot of pool games.  This one wins them all by virtue of completely believable physics, a fantastic, beautifully designed environment, and a focus on online gameplay.  As Foolinjection's review points out, there is no top-down veiw, keeping the gameplay as pure as possible. You can stand up and walk around the table, kneel down to check ball placements, but you must return and line up your shot the same way you would at a real pool table.
Pros -
-VooFoo is extremely well-versed in creating amazing looking, physics-true pool games.
-"Pure Pool" plays like its name. No cheat view to line up and shoot from the table lamp's eye of sight.
-The price for this game is VERY reasonable, even while not on sale!
-Rich focus on online gameplay.
-Achievements, trading cards, controller support!  (I play with gamepad and it is very functional and responsive)
-VooFoo DNA is a remarkable way to play against your friends or other challengers from online play, even when you are offline. It learns the play-style of players and is basically an AI version of that player!  Revolutionary! EXCELSIOR!
Cons-
-the UI is needing much improvement.
-inverted X axis on placing cue ball. There seems to be no workaround except for turning your brain into a mirror perspective when finding good placement on the table.
-unlike Hustle Kings, no option to play your music library instead of theirs, the cool jazzy soundtrack isn't horrible though, and you can always set the music volume down so you can pipe in your tunes from elsewhere.
-sometimes my connection to network isnt great, this is probably my janky DSL though.
(+EDIT+ seems to be the server. Lots of people complaining- devs need to update optimization)
-the game can prove to be pretty difficult if you are grinding for stars and achievements. Probably not a "con" for everyone,  but my wife gets stressed out when I've been cussing for an hour and a half about how all I want to do is pot two balls in the side pockets consecutively!
...and finally...
-you're reading this review,  and not playing it! Just get it, already!!
(EDIT)
Alright, after looking through forums on this game, it seems many people are having trouble with it. Either on the program itself working on their machines or on network gameplay. Lots of people having problems with controls and complaining about UI.  I do get where they are coming from, but I have hope that VooFoo and the publisher will be releasing optimization updates and patches for improving those situations, and hopefully an improvement to the UI is in the works.  Also there is only one venue for playing as of now.  I still insist that I'm having fun playing and still would recommend the game.

Heat Signature is yet another great little gem from Suspicious Developments. Although the game might not impress graphically, literally everything in the game screams deliberate design and every system has been carefully tuned to create a thrilling, unique, and highly replayable experience. This game is a masterclass in great system-based game design and empowering player agency, and I hope that developers learn from this game when deciding whether or not to make a unique game or churn out another microtransaction-bloated mobile port.

This is one of those games where you sit down to play a misson or two, and its 3 hours later.
I had been following this game ever since i saw the NerdCubed video on it (saw the Dan Hardcastle cameo btw) so when I noticed not only was it finally available, but on sale right away? Immediate purchase.
A lot of people are saying this is like if Hotline Miami were set in space, and to an extent, theyre right. You come into a level where you can see the enemies and the layout of the map, but the enemies cant see you, you go through and kill all the enemies, all dying in one shot. However, Heat Signature takes it a step above that. For starters, you don't die right away. One hit knocks you out, but then you get shot into space and are forced to catch yourself with your own spaceship flying at hundreds of miles an hour with the time ticking down and youre just a tiny little speck and oh dear god the panic. Secondly, you are at a slight advantage. You know the types of enemies you will fight, and you are allowed to bring whatever gear you think you will need into the fight. This being said, you are at a huge numbers disadvantage. There are 15 guards, 7 of them have shields, and you only have 3 charges on your shield dispelling gun. what now?
This scenario is where the game shines though. That "what now" moment is constant, and terrifying. You can try to get away, and just say screw it, ill come back when i have better gear. You can try to just stealth your way through, get your target and run. You can try to get a lucky drop in one of the ships cargo containers. Those are just the first few thoughts that go through your head.
As far as Ive seen, the combinations of weapons and gadgets in this game are what will make it the most replayable. One character I played as a pure brute shooter. When that eventually failed, I played as her father, a time altering ninja who went on a daring quest to get his daughter back (this was not a headcannon, this was the actual personal story i got with this character). Then when he eventually met his icy death, i played as a teleporting renegade, looking to avenge his sisters death. I would place down a glitch mine, that teleports your enemies to whereever you select, then I would swap my position with the enemy, shooting them directly into space, and me through the door. This was all within the 3 hours ive played just today.
In summary: this game gives you a character with a history and a personal quest, and tells you to do whatever missions you want to do in order to reach your goal. Its fast paced, you feel like a badass, and i can already tell, there is a lot of potential for "holy ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥ that actually worked???" moments. People might be saying that i can get repetitive, but I disagree. The amount of variation in the enemies alone make the game feel new each time you accept a contract. Add in the huge amount of ship layouts, loadouts, playstyles, and weapon variation, and i can easily see myself playing this game for days.
Alright hype, you win this time.

Heat Signature is essentially a "perma-death" heist/mercenary sandbox with a little depth and complexity. This game has no over-arching plot. There is no evil villain in the end. Instead, you progress by trying to capture all the stations in the galaxy. You unlock stations by doing missions, which comprise you flying to a ship in space, attaching to the side secretly, and completing whatever your contract may be (There are also personal missions you can do, though they serve no purpose other than recieving a weapon in return. You can name it whatever you want and your friends can find it. These aren't easy). As you unlock stations, not only do you unlock different tools, ships, and accessories that will help you as you try to progress, but also unlock new requirements for missions. These usually require you to use non-lethal weapons, not be spotted, leave no witnesses, etc. Practically every item you can unlock can already be found as you explore the galaxy and open crates in ships. However, they often have a limited amount of uses. Depending on how long your character has lived and what they have achieved, you will be able to progress at a faster rate. You keep trying to progress until your character is killed (in combat or space), captured (If you set off the alarm in the ship you are "raiding," they will fly to the nearest station of whatever faction they are a part of. If you are still in the ship when it arrives, you lose your character. You or your friends can save him later though.), or willingly retires. As you can already guess, you will die
That being said, it's still addicting as you try to progress.
As great as Heat Signature premise is, I believe it has a few problems. I'd like to mention these are entirely subjective (I am aware they have a small development team. I'm disregarding this for now, since I'm just wanting to regard issues I believe it has. I'm not expecting instant content updates soon). Many might not have problems with these and I will try to provide solutions that can fix these problems for me.

This game is an absolute must have. It's like Grand Theft Auto 1 and Gunpoint had a lovechild, and that lovechild blasted off into space for interstellar shenanigans. It makes really good use of procedural generation by maintaining a feeling of handcrafted designs at the same time as it gives us an abundance of content.
Flying around in your breaching pod is a lot of fun once you get the hang of the controls. Breaching spaceships is satisfying, and you're always in control over what sort of ships you feel like breaching thanks to missions clearly indicating what you'll encounter prior to accepting them. As the game progresses, the range of procedurally generated spaceships you are capable of successfully infiltrating increases, and so too does the range crazy things that can happen. Every bad situation you get yourself into always almost always has a way out of it... if you can pull it off.
Heat Signature has the most satisfying deaths I've experienced in a game that has permadeath. It manages to find the perfect balance between the thrills of rogue-like permadeath, and a system that lets you progress so that your time isn't completely up in smoke every time your character gets killed. The way meta-progression works in Heat Signature makes absolute sense. Any individual character can be killed if things go wrong, but each character is playing their own part in a wider struggle to liberate stations across the nebula. Whatever stations they liberated, help those who follow them in taking up the cause. This results in each encounter having a feeling of risk and excitement, while each death has still put you further ahead in a wider struggle. It's very nice to see meta-progression so seamlesly executed.
The combat is easy to get into, but tricky to master. it starts off fun and continues to get more and more enjoyable with every new station unlocked. The pause menu is a key part of fighting, and the game is very tactical because of this. It's about leaning heavily on whatever items you have in your inventory and using them as best as you can. Some are limited use, so conserving those becomes a strategic choice. Planning ahead, carefully choosing the right equipment, and coming up with tactics to deal with the various things you can encounter can feel particularly satisfying. But if you don't feel like planning ahead, then just rushing in and seeing what a beautiful mess you can make of things has its own rewards.
There are ususally multiple ways to tackle any situation. Heat Signature rewards experimentation. Regardless of your playstyle, things can go horribly wrong at any moment, forcing you to think on your feat. As the developer stated, Heat Signature is about getting yourself into messed up situations, and then figuring out how to get yourself out of them in once piece.
The only criticism that I can throw at it is that the mission select console's zoom-pan out to a wide shot of the nebula can sometimes be janky and result in missions not being displayed the first time. But, it's such a minor thing and everything else about the game is so good.
It's one of those rare games where players + procedural generation = an absolute gem of a game that's way more than the sum of its parts.

Cold, cruel, dark... how do I describe this game? No, this story? I just hope for one thing, and that is that no one has to ever experience the kind of emotional suffering involved for people in real life with real life decisions like choosing between lives to save or between your own welfare and your children's. No human should have to be forced to make those kinds of decisions. But that is exactly what this game forces you to do. Sure, you can stay silent during conversations, but you'll lose all respect.
I played all five episodes, one each day, and I've just finished the last one. And I feel like I really don't want to play another Season. This game is not hard, it's brutal. I think about things like the apocalypse a lot, like what a world full of the living dead will be like, or a world where only you are alive. This game had me questioning, as I still do, the worth and value of human existence in times of prolonged suffering. Is there hope? Real hope? Or is that simply a mental mechanism to keep going and find a reason, however illogical, to keep living. What is the purpose of life, what are we living for? To raise up children, to just enjoy ourselves, to keep moving towards the inevitability of death? However unreal and farcical you may think a zombie apocalypse is, it acts as a compelling context for life questions.
And not just that. It serves to seek out how we might react in a certain situation. Everyone has different personalities, and I'm sure you'd agree with me when I suggest that in this modern society, it's difficult to really know someone within a few days of meeting them. But when the world goes to absolute sh*t, there is no need for false impressions anymore. You can see people pretty square on. I had my brain in agony deciding, at times, what to say. I found myself trying to protect Clementine as much as I could. I realised her deepest desire was to see her parents, and I kept that in mind. I tried to save whoever I could. I saw people as humans, I saw them beneath their often capricious personalities (Kenny, Larry, Lilly - heh, even me sometimes). I tried to keep a level head all the time, and I guess that goes with my own underlying scepticism of life, held together by vocally agreeing with people who are good by their actions. I defined good as judging people not by what I or even our group needs, but by what the person being judged actually says they need. I could cite several situations, but I note this is a review, for those yet to buy the game.
I'm glad, now looking at the game as a whole, that TellTale didn't do a 'Last of Us'. Not only is this game true to the comic book foundations of TWD, but it meant that more resources can go into making a fantastic decision-based story that feels so real and just draws you into it. Yes, you are not Lee Everett, you don't have his history, his family, or even his words (talking about the choices of dialogue you get), but it's close enough to identifying what kind of a person YOU are, because each dialogue option takes a certain philosophy and moral direction. Mostly, I was consistent, but sometimes, such as with Larry, I blew. I could talk a lot about what this game teaches you, or has taught me, but I must restrain myself, knowing not to let a review become an essay in philosophical thought.
I haven't played anything like this before. It's different, and it's intelligent, and it will make you, yes, force you, to really think about what you say and do.

Alright normally I do not write reviews for video games. Going ahead with this I should feel that I say that I ABSOLUTELY with a burning passion hate MOBA's. This game turns my opinion on it's head. The game itself is solid, there are a few things I would do differently but I understand the way they are.
Pros-
-The game is beautifully optimized on the Unreal Engine, on medium settings the game still looks gorgeous despite me using an outdated video card.
-The game itself is balanced however teamwork IS AN ABSOLUTE MUST. Communication, strategy, concentration of fire are going to win the day.
-Teamwork is VERY rewarding
-Ships are unique in their roles, no two ships play the same, from long range supression bombardment or surprise missle attacks.
-Voice acting is great, the crews feel unique and the fact each crewmen has their own backstory and profile really gives me a feel for my crew.
-NO PAY TO WIN.
Cons-
-Pay to not grind which in itself is not a bad thing mind you. but defeats can be quite crushing when you don't have a booster and you make a meager amount of credits. Thankfully repair bills are not a thing.
-Very lack luster amount of maps at the time of this review. so I am certain there are more maps coming.
-MMR system I feel that this is superfluous as it is not an accurate gauge of how good a player is, just a matter amount of their wins. If your team loses your MMR goes down. So you can do extremely well and still lose MMR ranking instead of going up. Not a huge deal breaker but feels silly to me.
Other than that I have no real gripes about the games. I would say about 90% of my games are solid and fun with the other 10% what you expect from an online PVP game, crushing defeats from an obviously more coordinated team.
Overall, the game is solid, the core mechanics are amazing, it's beautiful and plays fluidly. If you like large capital ships or even smaller scale capital ships n just like to blow things up in space. Grab some friends, team up and go blow the enemy to kingdom come!

Not sure why this game is getting so much hate, I found it immensely fun (despite some glaring shortcomings).
Graphics are obviously very minimalist/discrete, but I like this.
Gunplay is very tight and precise, one shot kills on heads, and body hits take only a few to kill, so you can't get away with just rolling into a danger zone without thinking. it does also mean that you kill a lot and die a lot, but insta-respawns make this ok and keep the energy up.. it reminds me of gungame on CS. I thought it was perfect.
That said, the map design is very hit or miss, I'd say about 30% of maps are awesome, but the other 70% are either HUGE - meaning long chore-like hike between spawn and action, or they are built of far to many non destructible blocks, constraining a really vital element to this game:
MINING.. this shifts the game from being a mindless and OK shooter into an awesome strategic battlefield-esque game in which the environment plays an important part of the fight.
Fortifications can be built (moats, walls, bunkers, sniper posts, destroy cover for enemy's, create cover for your team) and clever mines can be made (dig right into your enemy's stronghold, or into the objective hill, make tank traps).
COMMUNITY: it's not bad, but pretty dumb. lots of cowards (just base camping). People complain about "hackers", I can't say I've seen any actual hackers, just a few good players and lots of cry-babies.
I'll be trying out a clan, as I think the ability to manipulate the environment like this would make a properly coordinated team effort pretty awesome.
RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THE DEVELOPERS:
- Defaults to Russian Servers. This should be IP dependent. I don't speak russian.
- Some totally crap and self indulgent maps, way too big, ornamental, or too many immovable blocks.
- environment ceiling is frequently set too low, constraining gameplay if you want to run across roofs.
- Jumping up single block steps is a pain, this should be auto-run to make moving around the map smoother
- Shouldn't be allowed to dig the floor immediately under spawn points (although funny when its happened, it does ruin that game)
-There should be a post-game screen so we can see scores and $hit-talk
- points gained by possessing the hill should be shown as individual score as well as team score.
- There should be pointers/descriptions on screen explaining game rules. I was frequently one of only 2-3 on teams who actually seemed to know what the objective of the game was.
- hitting escape should bring up the key bindings & map/game rules.
-Tanks need better sound effects
- hand held rocket launchers should be more powerful against tanks (as ammo for them is very valuable)
- Sound should be in 3D, this would make the underground mining battles much more strategic / fun.
- Get some server-specific voice servers so we can speak to each other
- some of the people with purchased upgrades were so powerful/strong that it really spoilt the gameplay. Be careful with this.
-There was a bug where the shotgun didn't seem to hurt anyone.
- introduce squad-based respawning or defibing like in battlefield, this would encourage cooperation more. As it is, death + the long hike back to the battlefield kills the energy of firefights.
With the current model of selling in game upgrades, having no real presence outside steam and generally coming across as a little scammy, I don't think it'll get that big, which is a shame, as I think it's got a lot of potential and I've had some great fun playing it.

This is one of those games where you sit down to play a misson or two, and its 3 hours later.
I had been following this game ever since i saw the NerdCubed video on it (saw the Dan Hardcastle cameo btw) so when I noticed not only was it finally available, but on sale right away? Immediate purchase.
A lot of people are saying this is like if Hotline Miami were set in space, and to an extent, theyre right. You come into a level where you can see the enemies and the layout of the map, but the enemies cant see you, you go through and kill all the enemies, all dying in one shot. However, Heat Signature takes it a step above that. For starters, you don't die right away. One hit knocks you out, but then you get shot into space and are forced to catch yourself with your own spaceship flying at hundreds of miles an hour with the time ticking down and youre just a tiny little speck and oh dear god the panic. Secondly, you are at a slight advantage. You know the types of enemies you will fight, and you are allowed to bring whatever gear you think you will need into the fight. This being said, you are at a huge numbers disadvantage. There are 15 guards, 7 of them have shields, and you only have 3 charges on your shield dispelling gun. what now?
This scenario is where the game shines though. That "what now" moment is constant, and terrifying. You can try to get away, and just say screw it, ill come back when i have better gear. You can try to just stealth your way through, get your target and run. You can try to get a lucky drop in one of the ships cargo containers. Those are just the first few thoughts that go through your head.
As far as Ive seen, the combinations of weapons and gadgets in this game are what will make it the most replayable. One character I played as a pure brute shooter. When that eventually failed, I played as her father, a time altering ninja who went on a daring quest to get his daughter back (this was not a headcannon, this was the actual personal story i got with this character). Then when he eventually met his icy death, i played as a teleporting renegade, looking to avenge his sisters death. I would place down a glitch mine, that teleports your enemies to whereever you select, then I would swap my position with the enemy, shooting them directly into space, and me through the door. This was all within the 3 hours ive played just today.
In summary: this game gives you a character with a history and a personal quest, and tells you to do whatever missions you want to do in order to reach your goal. Its fast paced, you feel like a badass, and i can already tell, there is a lot of potential for "holy ♥♥♥♥ing♥♥♥♥♥♥ that actually worked???" moments. People might be saying that i can get repetitive, but I disagree. The amount of variation in the enemies alone make the game feel new each time you accept a contract. Add in the huge amount of ship layouts, loadouts, playstyles, and weapon variation, and i can easily see myself playing this game for days.

Heat Signature is essentially a "perma-death" heist/mercenary sandbox with a little depth and complexity. This game has no over-arching plot. There is no evil villain in the end. Instead, you progress by trying to capture all the stations in the galaxy. You unlock stations by doing missions, which comprise you flying to a ship in space, attaching to the side secretly, and completing whatever your contract may be (There are also personal missions you can do, though they serve no purpose other than recieving a weapon in return. You can name it whatever you want and your friends can find it. These aren't easy). As you unlock stations, not only do you unlock different tools, ships, and accessories that will help you as you try to progress, but also unlock new requirements for missions. These usually require you to use non-lethal weapons, not be spotted, leave no witnesses, etc. Practically every item you can unlock can already be found as you explore the galaxy and open crates in ships. However, they often have a limited amount of uses. Depending on how long your character has lived and what they have achieved, you will be able to progress at a faster rate. You keep trying to progress until your character is killed (in combat or space), captured (If you set off the alarm in the ship you are "raiding," they will fly to the nearest station of whatever faction they are a part of. If you are still in the ship when it arrives, you lose your character. You or your friends can save him later though.), or willingly retires. As you can already guess, you will die
That being said, it's still addicting as you try to progress.
As great as Heat Signature premise is, I believe it has a few problems. I'd like to mention these are entirely subjective (I am aware they have a small development team. I'm disregarding this for now, since I'm just wanting to regard issues I believe it has. I'm not expecting instant content updates soon). Many might not have problems with these and I will try to provide solutions that can fix these problems for me.
It's like a poorly coded dark souls. That said if you can deal with that it's a pretty good game but i'd say just stick with dark souls.

This game is an absolute must have. It's like Grand Theft Auto 1 and Gunpoint had a lovechild, and that lovechild blasted off into space for interstellar shenanigans. It makes really good use of procedural generation by maintaining a feeling of handcrafted designs at the same time as it gives us an abundance of content.
Flying around in your breaching pod is a lot of fun once you get the hang of the controls. Breaching spaceships is satisfying, and you're always in control over what sort of ships you feel like breaching thanks to missions clearly indicating what you'll encounter prior to accepting them. As the game progresses, the range of procedurally generated spaceships you are capable of successfully infiltrating increases, and so too does the range crazy things that can happen. Every bad situation you get yourself into always almost always has a way out of it... if you can pull it off.
Heat Signature has the most satisfying deaths I've experienced in a game that has permadeath. It manages to find the perfect balance between the thrills of rogue-like permadeath, and a system that lets you progress so that your time isn't completely up in smoke every time your character gets killed. The way meta-progression works in Heat Signature makes absolute sense. Any individual character can be killed if things go wrong, but each character is playing their own part in a wider struggle to liberate stations across the nebula. Whatever stations they liberated, help those who follow them in taking up the cause. This results in each encounter having a feeling of risk and excitement, while each death has still put you further ahead in a wider struggle. It's very nice to see meta-progression so seamlesly executed.
The combat is easy to get into, but tricky to master. it starts off fun and continues to get more and more enjoyable with every new station unlocked. The pause menu is a key part of fighting, and the game is very tactical because of this. It's about leaning heavily on whatever items you have in your inventory and using them as best as you can. Some are limited use, so conserving those becomes a strategic choice. Planning ahead, carefully choosing the right equipment, and coming up with tactics to deal with the various things you can encounter can feel particularly satisfying. But if you don't feel like planning ahead, then just rushing in and seeing what a beautiful mess you can make of things has its own rewards.
There are ususally multiple ways to tackle any situation. Heat Signature rewards experimentation. Regardless of your playstyle, things can go horribly wrong at any moment, forcing you to think on your feat. As the developer stated, Heat Signature is about getting yourself into messed up situations, and then figuring out how to get yourself out of them in once piece.
The only criticism that I can throw at it is that the mission select console's zoom-pan out to a wide shot of the nebula can sometimes be janky and result in missions not being displayed the first time. But, it's such a minor thing and everything else about the game is so good.
It's one of those rare games where players + procedural generation = an absolute gem of a game that's way more than the sum of its parts.

If you haven't already downloaded this game, you are missing out on something magical. Almost everything (except CERTAIN exclusive SKINS) is unlockable through gameplay; and what's more, you're not going to grind for days just to get one ship or an upgrade. I play for 2-4 hours a night and have bought a ship, upgrades for my stock ships, cards, all kinds of stuff. All from my in-game credits.
That said, so far the additional cards and weapon mods don't really give players a specific edge, more like situational bonuses. I usually pilot a Reaper. the reaper is fast and has a ot of munitions, but it's definitely built for medium-range combat, and has a specific purpose of being a sniper killer. I can change my weapons so they do more damage to heavy hulls, or fire quicker to with less damage to protect ymself from lighter ships, and let my beam weapon do the talking on biger ships. The reaper gets a shield that protects its behind so that those attacking you as you pass them can't do as much damage. I can augment that so that it will protect me all over for a short period of time, or change it to top and bottom instead of behind. There's no augment available for my weaponry where I gain superlasers that deal massive damage with pinpoint accuracy, or shields that can soak massive damage all over. Everything is situational, and that's awesome because it really means that merit is based on skill and not on cash spent. In fact, even if you unlock all 31 ships, buy a bunch of platinum, etc, you'd still have to learn each one. Think about unlocking every single champion in LoL. You'd never play through all of them, and even if you did you'd never be awesome with all of them.
Now, outside of all of the F2P drama of the current gaming generation, this game is solid. I feel like I'm piloting a spaceship; your ship is slow, and yet there's moments where everything is over too fast. There hasn't been a game where either side was steamrolled, and lots of times where a team has come back from the brink because of poor planning on the opponents' part. Communication is vital here. There's no such thing as carrying your team. Either you work together or you lose, and there are certain comps that strengthen this. There is no ship that can take a sector by itself; double kills are things of amazement.
The aesthetic is just amazing. The first cinematic shows the ship up close and you really get a sense of scale for these things. It really sticks with you as you picture the battles from the cockpit. I actually really wish they'd allow for a "cockpit view" so you could watch this mountain of a spaceship fire a plasma ball at you the size of a skyscraper.
Literally my only complaint is for more maps and play types. The maps switch up, there's different styles of sector you can jump to (some are asteroids, some are long skinny rocks, some are more empty than others, etc), but I'd like to see different layouts. I think a capture the flag mode would be EXCELLENT.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

I found it to be a great story. Lots of ups and downs. I don't really like horror so I didn't like the handful of jump scares. However, it's not really overused so it was bearable. I ended up taking breaks in between scenes because I became invested in the story and a lot of heavy stuff happens. There was so much action/conflict that I enjoyed the slow, peaceful sequences where you could explore, talk, and solve simple puzzles.
Dialogue options have enough variety if you're trying to follow the story. Your options are limited in a way that you can't derail the plot so someone looking to test the limits or has too high expectations of freedom may become frustrated. My take on it is that it offers a good story as a backbone and your choices just help flesh out the details.
The dialogue timer often forces you have to pick based on instinct. I found it nice because not only was I engaged with the story, I had to chose what I would do in real time (instead of metagame it). I still used the rewind function several times but I recommend doing your first playthrough blind and choosing options that match what you would do.
If english isn't your first language (or your reading and/or comprehension speed isn't fast enough) then you will have trouble on the faster timers. In the fast ones I was able to get through by skimming the responses, making a gut choice, and then reacting before the time ran out. However I do think there should be a casual mode that extends timers to accomodate for people who can't/are unwilling to make choices on the spot. (Edit: WD2's space bar to pause was a better solution than a casual mode)
I'd recommend to anyone looking for a good thriller/drama/horror story experience.

Review: 8/10
Summary:
I really enjoyed MyCareer and it got better, IMO, with the Sophmore year in the NBA. The only thing that brings it down is the lack of optimization and technical flaws. This being said, 2k16 is as addicting as the rest of them and all the negative reviews are a shame to me. Finally, Spike, I'm a caucasian middle-manager for production at a major auto-manufacturer, age 28, played ball my whole life, and really liked your story and the actors did a great job. No, an excellent job. I can't say another name that had such good voice acting and direction, regardless of how it was accomplished. One day it will be appreciated fully.
MyCareer:
I loved MyCareer's story. Spike Lee did an excellent job writing and directing it - I was moved by the end of it and enthralled throughout. I also played basketball my entire life and enjoyed the sincerity in the script for many reasons: honest, truthful, and heavy. There was a constant reiteration of doing the right thing and the duality of Vic and Freq (you'll see) reallity struck home. No I didn't grow up in the projects of Harlem - but I also didn't crash land a space ship but I still play Endless Dungeon. The reviews, to me, were premature and it is a shame that this game has received such negativity in my opinion.
MyPark:
Different backgrounds and layouts but pretty much the same.
Gameplay and Control:
The most important thing to me in a video game is 'feel.' 2K delivers once again and gives an authentic and realistic portrayal of the game. I still believe that NBA 2K has created the best sports simulator to date!
Functionality:
The one thing that disappoints me is the lack of optimization and functionality; this is becoming a trend and an ultimate slap in the face to the PC gaming community from a vast range of developers. Bugs, crashes, and an inability to run on an aesthetically pleasing and entertaining level are essential to gameplay, but whether we like it or dimminish from it. Having to run on low just to be able to play the game is poor quality (running a GTX 980M) - but let me digress and say that I understand on consoles it is programming and optimizing on two or three platforms, not a virtually infinite combination of hardware and OS; I just hope 2K patches and improves it for the PC. I also fear that they may have already started working on 2k17 so the desire to continue investing in 2k products has taken a hit. I am still giving 2K the benefit of the doubt and much respect for attempting what majority of us could never produce on our own.
Final Comments:
Cannot stop playing! I love the game and am addicted, but show some love with a patch to make it even better, and improve the PC roster updating system to be live with the real season - especially trades! Please? :) Make the game better!

Stardew Valley... even mentioning the name to friends gets me excited to play again.  Stardew Valley gives something that you wouldn't expect, a nostalgic feeling of living on a quait farm. No matter which route you choose,  you will want to go as far as you can. Make friends with the villagers, rebuild the centerpiece of the town,  destroy the centerpiece of the town for better things, and try and make a name (or life) for yourself. This variety helps keep the game fresh, with five different map types and twelve different candidates to ask for their hand in marriage, you will find yourself wanting to play more and more. Sure, some of the tasks can be tedius, but no one said living life would be as simple as a click and shoot. All in all, the game is very solid, and the developer is still very active, going as far as working on a multiplayer mode, which is expected to release in early 2018.

So I decided to «thumb up» the game because I hope the developer would polish his game.
Planet RIX-13 pretends to be so called “old school pixel graphic point-n-click adventure”
There’re few puzzles in the game and they are rather simple so you don’t need to look for the game’s walkthrough.
The plot is a typical story about solving mysteries after the crash-landing on an alien planet abandon by humans. Planet RIX-13 is an extremely simple point-and-click adventure game.
Sadly, the game doesn’t really have much to say in the end, though it lasts less than an hour. It is basically a short story in game form, being almost purely linear in nature (you have an alternative ending here).
Graphically, it's exactly as presented at the screenshots.
I don’t like pixel graphics but even for me the game’s graphics is pretty nice.
There’s no music in the game at all and the developer used only three sounds in the game.
Nevertheless somehow the game gave me a sensation of the sci-fi atmosphere while I was playing it.
But even in this case you’d better buy it on sale because it’s too short.
Really it looks like a demo-version and you can’t expect more than an hour of gameplay.
By the way if you’re an achievement hunter Planet RIX-13 could be the next ideal game in your Steam profile.
______________________________________________________________
Так что я решил «поднять палец вверх» этой игре, потому что надеюсь на то, что разработчик отшлифует свою игру.
Планета РИКС-13 делает вид, что она – так называемая «пиксельная приключенческая игра старой школы».
В игре есть немного загадок и они довольно просты, так что вам не нужно будет искать прохождение этой игры.
Сюжет – это обычная история о решении тайн после аварийной посадки на чужой планете, заброшенной людьми. Планета РИКС-13 – чрезвычайно простая приключенческая игра.
К сожалению, игра немногое может поведать в конце, хотя ее продолжительность – меньше часа. Это в основном короткий рассказ в игровой форме, почти линейный по своей сути (у вас здесь есть альтернативная концовка).
Графически игра выглядит точно так, как представлено на скриншотах.
Мне не нравится пиксельная графика, но даже мне графика игры показалась приятной.
Музыки в игре нет (совсем) и разработчик использовал только три звука в игре.
Тем не менее, во время игры я каким-то образом ощущал научно-фантастическую атмосферу игры.
Но даже в этом случае вам лучше купить ее со скидкой, т.к. игра – слишком коротка.
На самом деле игра похожа на демо-версию, так что не ожидайте более часа геймплея.
Кстати, если вы охотник за достижениями, то Planet RIX-13 может стать следующей идеальной игрой в вашем профиле Steam.

Despite promises from Zen, many tables are NOT carried over from FX2 to FX3 (super league football, Plants vs Zombies and many, many others). Animation is noticeably more jerky and "slide-show" than FX2. Sometimes the ball moves so quickly across the table that the graphics engine doesn't have time to render all of the animation frames, and so the ball appears to "teleport" from one place to another. This makes it extremely difficult to follow the ball with your eyes, and makes it much harder to judge where the ball is actually going. Sometimes the game stutters and jerks for no accountable reasaon.
There are also annoying pop-ups which appear in the top-right of the screen during the game, which are unreadable. If you take your eyes off the ball in order to read the messages, it's 90% likely you'll lose the ball.
The user interface in the menus is awful. For example, if you click on the "single-player classic" category button to see your high score in that category, instead of showing you the high score, the screen gets cleared and a new game is started. You have to use the keyboard arrow keys to move the highlight to the required score category so you can see the info you want! There's also the annoying, speaking pop-up female "guide" who keeps jumping up with either unwanted or obvious messages, and you have to click "OK" with the mouse so she'll unblock the screen and let you get on with what you want to do.
As you might have guessed, I'm going back to FX2 where I can play ALL of the tables I've spent my money on, and where the animation is smooth, realistic, and playable. FX3 has been designed for magazine screen shots, not pinball players.

An excellent shmup that takes me back to playing similar games in arcades in the 90s.  Three characters to choose from, each with a singificantly different playstyle.  Multiple difficulty levels, the lowest of which should allow even casual players to see most of the game.
Very pretty pixel art and beautiful cabinet-style sidebars.
Controls are slightly unresponsive, but not so much as to detract from the game.  If you ever played an old arcade game with a well-maintained but 'sticky' joystick (pizza parlor Raiden), that's what it feels like.
A few caveats:
Don'Yoku is full screen by default and I haven't found a way to run it windowed.
More importantly, this game is shackled with the WORST default keybindings I have EVER seen.  At first, I was convinced the controls were broken.
Not only are the default bindings unintuitive (WASD + BNM, Controller support in menu only, no analog stick support, keyboard arrow keys do nothing), but they're also inconsistent.
It took a while, but once I'd set controls to joystick and rebound the action buttons, I had a great time with this game.
Highly recommended, IF you either have a gamepad and reconfigure the controls, OR don't mind a WASD keyboard setup.
