Super Hexagon 2: Revelations finally comes to Steam again and this time, it's personal.
You play as Commander Shephard in a fight to save humanity from geometry with rocks on strings.  You face off in the ultimate arena known only as "arcade."  This game is different from most games on the market because your decisions actually mean something, just like the original Super Hexagon (no TellTale here!).  For instance, the "score" in the bottom left corner isn't a score at all; it shows how many humans the combine will keep alive to enslave when they take over Pandora (the higher number the better btw).
The story is very complex.  There's tons of sexual tension between the rocks and a triangle, and you, the player, can decide where to put it.  Will you release the tension by having alien sex like in Star Effect, or will you build it up to become stronger like in 1984 by George Orwell.  Like I said, your decisions really affect the story, and the better decisions you make the more story you get.  But of course, the best decision you can make is to get this game.

It is a well fleshed out game for those that enjoy the grind and don't mind losing characters.  Losing characters is actually a fun and interesting part of the game, however, the grind is just too much for me.  Eventually you get stuck seeing the same enemies so many times that you go a little crazy yourelf.
The stress system in the game is great, and really is the part of the game that really makes it difficult.  Managing stress makes dungeon crawling fun for a while, but even that loses its luster when you realize how easy it is to manage if you plan for the dungeon you are in.  If I go in dungeon type X, it has Y type of enemies.  I will be dealing with a lot of stress, so I will bring Z type of champions.  Pretty simple.  If you have a good memory you will know what you will encounter in a dungeon.  If not, you can always look it up and prepare for the dungeon correctly.  (CAUTION: PREPARING CORRECTLY DOES NOT ALWAYS GIVE YOU SUCCESS, THE GAME IS NOT SET UP FOR YOU TO ALWAYS WIN.  NOTHING WRONG WITH THAT IN MY OPINION)
I didn't beat the game I'm sad to say, and would like to at some point but I'm afraid I just keep getting bored and deleting it from my library.
So, although I'm giving this game a negative review, I would like to say there are many players that I feel will enjoy this game.  If you are looking for a challenge, are willing to look up information on Wikis or have a good memory, and don't mind a constant dungeon grind, this game is 100% a good fit for you.  If you are impatient, bored easily, or have a poor memory/don't want to look up information, this game is not for you.
If you are part of the group that tries the game, I highly recommend gearing a party, not a solo troop.  Focus on everyone you have.  You never know when your best will need to be replaced.  Its part of the charm of the game, and is what kept me interested as long as it did, and is probaby why I will end up playing it again.   I hope this helps someone with their purchase in the future.
EDIT: I tried it again after a talk with another player, and have to say that Radient mode really made the game better.  Although it brought me some more joy, you still can find some of the same RNG things that I actually do enjoy.  I changed my review to a positive, especially if you try the game with workshop content.
However, if you do not like RNG games and you are easily attached to characters, you should stay away from this game.  You won't find joy here lol.

My GotY for 2016.  Favorite things:
-Stress system.  This is a perfectly designed lair to the roster management.  It forces you to rotate your party as your different characters need to take breaks, and ties in perfectly to the personality quirks that make the characters so memorable.
-Personality quirks.  There is a great mix of grim and sass in how the characters develop.  I love how they will rob your gold, get on a winning streak at the card table, refuse quests that are 'beneith them' and all the other personal touches the random quriks encourage.
-Party management.  The core of the combat is so so good. I was constantly drawn to mix-and-match all the different classes and abilities.  It kept me engaged and really scratched the same 'customizable experience' itch as Transistor and Hearthstone.
-The story.  The endgame content got just grindy enough at the end to turn me off, but it brought me back in with a very well executed story that marries everything you've been doing together.

Fresh take on the MOBA genre.  Typically not a MOBA player myself, ive found this to be enjoyable.  Its by no means perfect, but there is something very satisfying about its simple, yet deep game play.   The hardest challenge so far for me is finding a ship to upgrade to since I REALLY like the Pioneer starting ship.
PROS:
-Free to play
-Cash shop is above average for value/game play impact.  ($30 right now gets you every ship in the games roster), so the price of an indie title, well priced and fair.
-Grind isnt nearly as bad as other similar vehicle arena titles (about 10-15 matches and i could buy a mid price ship @ 300k)
-Good ship variety
-Skill based abilities and the capacity to take down a better ship with a lower "tier" ship if played properly
-Looks and runs great, good atmosphere
CONS
- Match making is done by MMR and not by ship selection (which happens post match making when the game is created), so you sometimes get out classed fairly bad in terms of ship quality.
- (Situational CON) Its easier to have the win robbed from under your feet with the way this games lane system works.  I say its situational because I beleive the sneaky counter attack option is a good tactic, but some players may get frustrated that you can be "base dived" easier here then most other MOBAs
All in all, solid Free to play, I could see myself getting 40-60 hours out of this.  Might even buy some stuff to support the developers rational pricing system.  **Glares at War Thunder for wanting $60 USD for one premium vehicle.....

This is a tough review to write because there are some things that are really great about this game and others that are really bad.  First of all, if you don't have a new nvidia card then dont even bother because it is not optimised for anything else.  I have a gtx 970 so i can play it pretty much maxed though.
I am going to talk about the my career mode mainly since thats all I have really played and it is pretty much what I buy 2k for.  The problem with this game is the story kind of ruins it.  Your family is black even if you make a white character and the story is really cheese and you don't actually get any choice in any big decisions for your character.  The cut scenes are 20 min long even though they could be summed up in a 1 min scene.  The story definitely affects your character too much.  You don't get to decide what type  of person you want your player to be- spike lee decides that for you.  He also decides that you will leave college after your first year even though they make such a big deal over what a huge decision it is.  One of the biggest issues is that you dont get to play your rookie year.  You only play 8 games and you have no chance to make the playoffs.  Also, your ratings in this game start out at the lowest ever.  only about a 50 overall.  And best of all, you make no vc at all for the high school or college games.  And since you only play 8 games in your first season, you pretty much go into your second season with that same rating.  I think that this is just greed on 2k's part trying to get you to buy vc because if you didnt preorder the game for the extra 10k vc and you are just playing from the starting rating it is really brutal to try and progresss.  It is basically like taking a middle school kid and throwing him in to play with professionals.  It is really annoying to see this happen in a game that I paid 60 bucks for.  And, after all this hype over the story, it ends after the first season.  The story really ♥♥♥♥ed up this game and I really think 2k should just give you an option to skip it entirely and just play your first season as normal.
So that is a lot of bad stuff so you would think that this would obviously be a negative review however there actaully is a lot of good stuff as well.  Mainly in terms of the actual gameplay which I feel is what matters most.  2k has fixed a lot of the cheese from previous years and I really do feel like the game plays a lot smoother now and all of the animations look a lot better.  The high school and college games are actually done extremley well even though you dont get to play many games.  There is a lot of little details that they took the time to add that really add to the realism of the high school and college games.  You also have a lot more options to customize your player.  The practice mode and the other options of how to spend your off days is a really nice touch except for the fact that the practice mode is stuck in a side view camera that you cannot change (2k PLEASE FIX THIS) which makes some of the drills pretty much unplayable.  I also really like that you have the ability to see contracts from 3 different teams and try to haggle with them to get more vc and minutes.  Another thing I will add is that, in my opinion, the music in this game is a lot better than in previous 2k games.
All in all, there is a lot of bad in this game but I do think 2k pulled through where it really matters which is in the actual gameplay.  And I think that the gameplay is actually so much better than every other 2k game that it makes up for the storyline cheese which is why I gave it a positive review.

You wake up to find your world in pieces. Wordlessly, you get up in search of the one place everyone has agreed to go to in times of trouble... The Bastion.
Bastion is an Action-RPG with an isometric point of view. You play as a white-haired youth only referred to as "The Kid," and traverse vast, various landscapes in search of "Cores" to power the Bastion.
Nowadays, it's tough to combine gameplay and story together without having the two separated from one another. Bastion solves that problem by the deft use of (incredibly deep and sexy) narration as you play the game, helped by Logan Cunningham's performance. Almost everything you do in-game will be commented on by the narrator. And the narration NEVER gets annoying.
Bastion is an excellent example of how a game can captivate the player with its engaging plot and intense gameplay. For those looking for an experience, Bastion will most certainly deliver.

A fun hack-n-slash RPG with interesting visuals, compelling narrative and
surprising amount of customization.  Each level you get a new weapon to use and the ability to upgrade with items you find along your quest or through winning challenges at the Proving Grounds.  You also get perks for your characters and crystal shards that grant the ability to rebuild your town with different shops and even a shrine where you can invoke the gods.  I like as you progress through each new area, the narrator makes interesting comments and unfolds the story for you, and at the end, you finally figure out what the calamity is all about.  There are a few annoying aspects such as you can't replay areas you've finished and whenever you pick up a new weapon you are unable to swap it out for one you're more use to.  Also, it's a pretty short game, probably around 9-10 for most people depending on how much time you want to spend leveling up.  Overall though, a great game woth playing.

A game about planning, executing, and then planning again after your first plan fumbled.
Heat Signature is developed by a company called Suspicious Decelopments, which is actually just the work of one man; Tom Francis.
Now onto the actual review...
Heat Signature is a highly skill based game involving infiltrating ships, and completing certain objectives from within. These objectives can range from assassinations, to heists. These missions are randomly generated based on certain parameters.
Difficulty is the overall difficulty of the mission, and affects everything from the size of the ship, to the amount and gear of the enemies.
Each mission also gives the enemy a different 'kit', which gives them abilities that range from heat sensors, to total immunity to damage. While some are obviously more difficult than others, there's always a way to circumvent, and with the correct gear, can actually make enemies with certain kits easier than without.
And finally, the objective. An objective is one of the few concrete things in a mission. And although there aren't too many different objectives, you'll be hard pressed to find the exact same mission twice. The way you can approach the objective is more akin to Dishonored then Hotline Miami. You could go in full Rambo, duel wielding quickfire shotguns to quickly dispose of waves of enemis, dodging bullets using the slow motion. You could use teleportation, and a stealth field to quietly reach your objective, only to swapper teleport into your pod, using the unconcious body you cleverly placed there.
The approaches to the different mission makes up for the few different objectives, and makes sure that each mission will feel different.
Now in terms of game mechanics, this game has it great. A big, and quite noticable feature, is the ability to slow time down in tough situations. This hammers home the game's emphasis on planning, and allows the player to plan and execute on the fly. And if that's not enough, you can also pause the game, allowing more time to plan. You can even start an action, like aim, or teleport while paused, allowing highly precise actions.
And speaking of teleporting, this game has a vast armory of different gadgets, all allowing almost endless veriety in the way you approach missions. This can range from a simple silenced pistol, to a slow motion device, to a gun that shoots everything. And most of these things can come with upgraded versions. Like a teleporter that recharges during the mission, or a keycard copy device that works at a massive distance.
Of course, all games must have cons, and in my opinion, this game has a few.
The art style is quite nice looking, and I love the look of the ships, but it's sometimes quite difficult to see enemies, or keycards on the ground. Keycards can just be teleported to you, but it can be a bit shocking for an enemy to suddenly appear in the seemingly empty room. This is more a problem with enemies without kits, but the multi colored armor of the Glitchers can be almost the exact same color of the equally multi colored rooms they're in.
Sometimes the mission generation can be a bit unfair. There was one instance in which all of my missions had armored enemies, but I didn't have an armor piercing weapon yet. It's almost always possible to complete a mission as such, but sometimes it's better to just abort a mission to get a new list.
Finally, the AI is mediocre. When they spot you, they're much better at searching for your location, but when they're idle, they have a nasty tendency to walk to terminals, all by themselves. This makes it possible to simply wait for an enemy to split, kill/knockout the enemy, hide the body, and then simply wait for the next guy to come in. Although it trivializes some stealth missions, the kits eventually made it much more difficult, and actually sometimes encouraged group fighting, in order to make the most of your own gadgets.
And finally, something that could be a bad thing to more than a few, and that's the difficulty.
The game can, at times, get very difficult. Fighting against enemies with impenetrable shields is one, but fighting shielded, teleporting enemies with shotguns, and turrets on every corner in a huge ship with a pacifist tag is around where this game takes some planning. Of course, by that point the player will have a character with many different gadgets on hand, and could kill with a glance - these missions can still prove troublesome. Luckily, you always can choose a different mission, and you are never forced into a mission that you wouldn't want to do. (Assassination mission with a non-lethal character, anyone?)
Overall, this game is great. It can be difficult at times, but the feeling of beating a mission which is even considered impossible in-game makes the feeling so much greater. I've yet to see a game make you feel like someone out of an action movie as well as this game.
Recommend this game for anyone who loves thinking on their toes, and enjoyed games like Hotline Miami, or Dishonored.

Ok, where to begin. FYI- this review isnt negative only because creation club issues, but rather game itself as well.
So lets take a look at most obvious (and newest) fault- creation club. Ok, you create framework where modders can sell stuff, okay, fine. I dont like the way its done, but go nuts. What i DONT tolerate in slightest, however, is that its forcibly downloading EVERY MOD, yet you CANNOT use them until you pay them. So that means there are essentially several gigs worth of data you are forced to download that serves absolutely no purpose at all UNLESS you pay for them. That is something thats simply unacceptable! Sure, space & data tend to be cheap nowadays, but still, this is more matter of principle. I'd rather use that space for just about anything. Heck, even hundreds of pictures of dry paint would be more useful.
But what about game itself? Its average at best, especially without mods. It does feel like move in right direction in many gameplay aspects, yet in most ways it lags far behind New Vegas. Also, several good ideas are not done very well. Like combat- it definetly feels like devs wanted to take more traditional FPS feel, but kinda stopped at half way & gunplay feels akward. On other hand, VATS doesnt pause game anymore, forcing you to think bit quicker, which is good thing.
Building is definetly not worth the hype- way too clunky. I also dislike direction they took with chat- its bit too simplified, i'd rather have old-styled chat. Still, voiced protagonist idea is something i actually do like (i know im in minority with this, but still, its good idea).
The loot menu is also akward- i like idea of quick scrapping, but again, the solution implemented feels akward as you can only see 2-3 items at once. So again, old style fits everything better.
But whats positive? Well, world does look nice and so far, lot of characters feel good. Quests (at least ones i've had) arent worst either, but then again, i havent progressed real far.
Still, lot of great mods are already out, although without full F4SE release, best mods wont arrive anytime soon

This game is a true example of how you do a sequel.
A brilliant mix and match of turn based strategy on one hand and base and soldier management on the other.  This game evokes the perfect feeling of just wanting to try 1 more mission as you unlock more and more stuff in the base for you to use in combat.  From a mech companion, new soldier ability, new gun and even new psychic abilities.
The story is well written and the pacing is good.  You learn about the world around you as you go along and as your scientists and technicians research new stuff you get about a page worth’s of lore to read if you want.  There is the occasional banter on your home base as well but you can ignore that for the most part.
The game has its bugs of course.  Sometimes the maps feel a little samey even though they are procedural and there have been the occasional AI glitch or graphical glitch but those aren’t a huge issue.
The game boasts modding support and it has a rather powerful set of tools for mod making.  If I can recommend any then go look at the Long War collection of mini mods.  All together they make for a rather fantastic set of mods to greatly expand your game.

The first time I played Particle Mace was at a PAX party last year, and I was fairly drunk.  When the social anxiety started to kick in, I grabbed another drink and shuffled over to where they had a few indie games set up to project against the walls, thinking that if I looked like I was engrossed in watching others play, no one would bother me.  People seemed most excited about a game that looked like some sort of colorful modern Astroids, except they were sling-shotting particles around and fighting with four players in a battle royale.  I don't really recall everything that happened that night, but at some point I had a controller in my hands and was playing Particle Mace against three others.  It was one of the most intense and fun gaming experiences I've ever had, and I somehow managed to outmanouver everyone and claim victory.
Yes this game is beautiful and silky-smooth fluid, but most of all it's SATISFYING.  Every time your particles smash into an astroid, enemy, or player, the game emphasises it in a way that scratches an itch I didn't know I had.
A++ would recommend especially as a (drunk) couch co-op game.

This hack and slash aRPG has the player controlling Kid, a youth surviving the events of the
. Said event destroyed much of the world that he knew and now he must traverse it, seeking to restore the Bastion. The Kid is a silent protagonist but the narrator following him around definitely isn’t. The narration is the main selling point of Bastion and where it got a lot of its praise from. The narrator’s deep tones are used to describe both the story, the interactions between characters and the player’s actions with an almost AI level of cognition. Falling off a ledge, getting hit by enemies, not figuring out where to go next gets either encouragement, prodding or almost sarcastic remarks from the narrator depending on the situation. But the narrator remains ever steadfast, determined to help the Kid out. It won’t comment on every single action taken but it’s enough to be interesting during this four hour or so campaign.
There's the Bastion level where you’re able to trigger parts of the story plot, customize the Kid’s weaponry and choose which level to go next. On each combat level is a piece of the Bastion (shards) that you must locate (usually hidden behind bosses) in order to reassemble and power it up. On combat levels, pieces of the level come falling down from the sky so you won't always know where to go next. I’m pretty mixed on this idea. I get that they didn’t want the entire level to be seen immediately nor wanted to use darkness to hide it, but it often leads to you running into walls a lot of the time.
Combat is a repetitive hack-and-slash with guns, hammers, blades and many other assorted weapons. Kid can only have two weapons equipped along with a special ability. The special ability can be summonable monsters to special weapon attacks and require dark potions to use. The Kid can’t recover his health over time, so the player will need to keep an eye out for health potions and use them when low on health. There’s an upgrade tree for weapons that changes the ability and strength to the player’s preference. It’s a good idea to figure out what weapons you’ll like early on. Each weapon upgrade requires a unique material as well as a number of spirits/currency in order to be applied. The currency can take a while unless you wish to grind the proving ground or monster waves (remembrance) level. There's also collectible items (Mementos), Vigils that change monster behavior and stats for increasing your risk/reward. All of which help take the edge off the repetitiveness of Bastion but only a little bit. For the most part, I found I ended up setting these to what I preferred and forgetting them. Unless you visit the challenge levels and complete them for the rewards, there's not a lot to choose from in the normal course of the game.
Combat is pretty solid though the main problem is definitely the lacking variety of enemies. You’ll see the majority of them pretty early on and they get reused a lot. The way to defeat them is also pretty samey. Line up a shot, hopefully triggering a power-shot which gives it an extra boost, dodge out of the way if the enemy gets too close and shoot again. Rinse and repeat. A lot of the time it can feel like long battles of attrition between the health potions and seemingly endless stream of monsters.
Bastion has a reasonable selection of options to customize the experience. It does give you a selection of resolution options depending on your aspect ratio. Though anything outside of a 16:9 resolution will be letterboxed. Fullscreen is on/off though you can force borderless windowed mode through a launch option. Read about how to do that on
. Visual settings are extremely limited to vertical sync on/off and anti-aliasing up to 4x. I’ll grant that it’s a 2D game so lots of graphical options are probably unnecessary. However, Bastion makes up for it with a plentiful audio menu. (Where the brightness slider is located, strangely). Music, FX and narration volume can all be adjusted here with sliders for each individual one. Keyboard, mouse and controller are all supported for Bastion though controller seems to be the preferred method.
Bastion still holds up as a good looking indie title with its cartoony, colorful visual style. A style that has been very well implemented and holds up all game. The soundtrack is very well done and remains one of my favorite albums from gaming. I recommend
after you've finished playing the game.
Bastion is a solid experience from beginning to end. The narration is very well done, constantly keeping the player engaged and not getting overbearing or annoying. The story and combat are both solid and reasonably enjoyable for the short experience. Though I do feel like the customization/crafting system requires a bit too much grinding and the combat system can feel far too repetitive at times due to the small pool of enemies. Still, I think it's worth giving Bastion a look over, even after all this time.

After about 100 hours sinked into Darkest Dungeon, I finally feel ready to write a review.
Let's get the hard one out of the way and talk about the elephant in the room: the RNG (Random Number Generator, or the game equivalent of luck). Yes, the game is heavily (but NOT completely) based on RNG. Yes, you can never be 100% prepared for every outcome of every round in every battle. And yes, that WILL make you extremely salty at times.
Whether or not Darkest Dungeon will be an enjoyable experience to you depends a lot on how offended you are by being screwed by random odds every now and then, and how resistent you are to seek help on wikis and the like. I usually go fully blind (i.e. without looking at any guides), but for this game in particular that is just masochism. Prior knowledge of what you are about to face makes all the difference in the world here, so going completely blind will make your life a hell of a lot more difficult. Many people also complain about excessive grinding but that is not really true. The game offers an "anti-grind mode" (Radiant Mode, which is NOT the same as an "Easy Mode") and lots of people complete it in 20-30 hours, something pretty standard for RPGs.
As you might know (or have noticed) already, the developers WANT their game to be like this. Their are willing to sacrifice the common notion of good game design for the sake of the difficulty, for the sake of bringing you to the brink of desperation. That is part of this game's appeal. Take it for what it is... or don't. When you make a deal with the devil you gotta know what you're singing in for.
As for everything else, the  soundtrack and atmosphere are simply astonishing (in my opinion of course). The narrator never gets old, and the many team and enemy composions keep the gameplay fresh for a very long time.

Half-Life is definitely not for everyone, not today when players are not used to outdated graphics and higher difficulty. It's undoubtedly a great game. It's different from everything I've ever played. I decided to play it on medium difficulty because why not? I am used to playing shooters after all. Hell, it was so frustrating, sometimes. Not because the enemies would be that hard to kill, they were not, but because I got lost and didn't know how to continue and while I was going through all the rooms again to find my way out, I fell down here, lost a bit health there and after some time I couldn't continue without loading an older save to try to play that part again and to be more careful this time.
In chapter 6, Blast Pit, I totally lost clue about what to do next. I was struggling to motivate myself to keep playing. But then I found those amazing walkthrough videos made by BigMacDavis and he and his love for Half-Life made me want to continue. I really have to recommended them because it helps you, it's fun and very nice to listen to.
After chapter 6 I started to love the game more and more. I got several new weapons, also unique ones, which were fun to use and very effective. The use of different weapons for different enemies was very satisfying. Valve did a really good job there.
If you like sci-fi and shooters and don't care about nicest graphics. If you want action without too many dialogues and if you don't get easily frustrated. Or if you just want to know why this game is so popular, give it a chance. It's worth of it!

I love this game.
Emergent gameplay done right is hard to find, but you can find it here.. Let me tell you a story.
My mission was to rescue a guy from on board an enemy ship, but still being relatively new to the game at the time, I didn't know the armor of the guards on the ship would be too strong for any weapons I had in my posession at the time.
I decided to make my way through this HUGE ship without picking up any of the keycards, because I didn't have a keycloner, or a weapon capable of taking out the armored guards... I had a self-recharging Sidewinder (teleporter that teleports you anywhere within range, as long as there is an unbroken path between you and the destination..) and a crappy little pistol.
I was using the pistol to fire a few shots to lure guards toward a door, running away from the door, then teleporting to a place on the other side of the now-open door and continuing on.  On board the ship, I located a Subverter, which made dealing with the stationary turrets a lot less stressful, and I eventually made my way to my target, only to be faced with a new problem... I didn't have any keycards, so how do I get out?
I formulated a plan.. two rooms away was a room with a window... using a clever combination of shooting, teleporting, carrying my rescue target around to different places, luring guards, and getting a few more doors open, while also taking my objective with me, I find myself in the room with the window finally.. except after I teleported, I mis-clicked and accidentally fired a round, which attracted the attention of the guards.
As soon as my gun was ready to fire again, and the enemy guards were pouring into the room while I stood in the corner, I shot the window and flung myself, my objective, and 3 or 4 enemies out into the vaccuum of space, due to the sudden decompression..  I pull up my menu, select my pod, and remote controlled it to scoop up my objective, then myself before we ran out of air, then burned out of there and back to a friendly base.
That's just one of many stories I already have from this game.  9/10 game automatically already, simply because you CAN'T get a gameplay experience like that just anywhere, it takes a special, rare game, and this is one of them.  It's also really well made, the music sounds nice, and the mechanics of the game all just work together so dang well I can't help but give this a full recommendation.

I'll preface this by saying Fallout 4 WAS a fantastic game, probably my favorite of all the Bethesda Fallout titles.
With that out of the way, the addition of Bethesda's "Creation Club" which is paid mods at best, or microtransactions in a single player RPG at worst, the game has all but been ruined. In addition to adding more bugs to the game, the opposite of what the company promised, as well as Bethesda breaking their promise of pure, original content which was broken day 1 by them recycling old content rom previous games and ripping off mods already found online for free.
All of this would mean nothing to me if the Creation Club was something I signed up for, but as it stands any update to the Creation Club will update your fallout 4 and add more files on your disk drive, EVEN IF YOU DO NOT WISH TO DOWNLOAD ANY OF THAT CONTENT. This means the Creation club eats up more disk space with every update. In addition, the constant updates to the executeable means that the Fallout 4 Script Editor, which is fundementally important for several mods that FIX PROBLEMS BETHESDA LEFT IN THE GAME AND STILL HAVE YET TO FIX.
In doing this Bethesda has actively taken a swing at their own community and is trying to exploit something that has been free for years for a little extra money. Supporting Bethesda in any way until they reverse this choice is harmful to the video game industry.

In comparing games and game systems, the refrain "Graphics don't matter," is typically just the fallback cry of the partisan whose favoured game or system has demonstrably inferior graphics.
is one of the rare games that proves the phrase correct.
Graphically,
is an obvious direct descendant of the original vectored
, just prettied up a little.  Instead of pivot-and-shoot gameplay, however, your gunless ship battles by dragging little objects around on tethers, and using inertia to swing them around.  It's a fairly simple concept, but the game keeps it from getting stale too quickly by gradually introducing variant ships with slightly different performance characteristics, and missions (challenges, really) that provide twists on the core gameplay.
is a simple but addictive game.  Part of the secret of the addictiveness is that the game gradually gets harder, but is scrupulously fair.  It gives that "one more try" feeling because, when you die -- and you die a
-- the death always feels like your fault.  I've yet to have a death in this game feel like the game cheated or presented an impossible situation; I always get the sense that if I'd only played a little bit better, I might have triumphed, and that draws me back for another round.

This is one of those games that just gets better as it updates! As of this review [7/16/16] The new quasi-quest system (I say that because it isn't like a traditional MMO-RPG or something) and the addition of mowing down renegade techs is pretty entertaining. The parts are relatively easy to come by, simply mow-down your opponent steal bits from his tech, and drive away from the smoking ruins.
I love that the parts will explode if they take too much damage, which forces the player to try and fight more tactically, sort of. It really boils down to hoping your automated guns destroy his cab before the rest of his tech gets destroyed. However, if you're anything like me, you're probabbly just gonna obliterate the other guy and pick up some scraps.
The game even makes resource collection fun, in that you have to attach tractor-beams to your vehicle and collect chunks of resources as you explore the planet and mow-down other vehicles. [Side note, I used to think they were robots]
All in all a solid game that has some very competent creators!

TL;DR I would recommend buying this game ONLY if you meet the minimum Requirements. This game is very enjoyable even on low settings with beautiful scenery.
Anyone who says there are technical bugs, are really just butt hurt they can't play it above medium settings. I bought this game with an I3 and an AMD 7770, It ran at at least 18 - 20 fps and I constantly had bugs .. Then patch 4 came out! And I saw an increase in 2 fps. So they obviously did something. I ran it on low settings, and beat the campaign. Not very thrilled that I went from black flag high settings to low settings on Unity, but it didn't bother me....
But then I upgraded and holy crap. I replayed this game just for the simple fact that I upgraded. I am now running an i5 overclocked at 3.4 and a GTX 770. The difference it made was phenomenal. I can now run this game at medium settings straight with 45-50 fps in streets and 60 fps no problem on the roofs. On top of this, now amazing looking game, the story line was very solid. It honestly reminded me a lot of Assassins Creed 2 so I hope for a sequel with Arno.
I believe this game has made advances with the mechanics, I love the way you can now control the way Arno free runs. This really drove me nuts in other games that I could control the decent. I just had to manually jump and kind of hope for the best..
Well, to make a long review short I'm going to keep it simple and end it here. 4/10 before patches and upgrade 9/10 after. Yes, I will agree this game is very demanding and really has no reason to be, I would counter argue with the fact that this game is massive. A 1 to 1 scale has never been done in a game before and this one captures it perfectly. Flying from roof to roof with my assassins buddies couldn't get anymore fun. I would recommend buying this game ONLY if you meet the minimum Requirements. This game is very enjoyable even on low settings with beautiful scenery.

A fun game with a lot of promise, Starbound has enough content and enjoyment that I was not disappointed in playing it. However my dissapointment comes from the promise that Starbound and its development once had, now bogged down in a lack of updates and content that has never evolved past the "early access" it is supposed to move forward from. On the one hand I had a lot of fun with my "Terraria in space", but on the other hand this is the game that put me off on the concept of "early access" as a whole.
UPDATE MAY 10 2015
Alright, I decided to give Starbound another go, so let's have a Revisit Review.
So, in terms of stuff they have added, there have been improved microdungeons (a lot more common with some unique stuff to find), as well as a streamlined progression; The game is a lot more linear than it previously was but the upside to this is that there is a lot more focus. You have missions to complete, boss levels you can work on, and some unique areas to visit from this. The downside of this is that the open-endedness of the game is lost, and as such you essentially HAVE to follow the path the game gives you in order to progress; You can't go onto irradiated worlds that have the ores you need until you complete mission A, B, and C in that order.
There is also an interesting hub area in the game, an outpost area that provides smaller missions  and the main ones as well, as well as opportunities to buy certain items from shops. This area is nice but feels tacked on at this point, as apart from the missions the items there (with the exception of the signs and the teleporters) are pretty much common.
Hunger and temperature have been removed from the game, which I feel the game is less for. With the aforementioned missions giving you the "shield" to arbitrarily protect you from cold or heat, with going on these planets without the shield being boiled down to the same status effect as the poison. Without hunger too the food feels a lot less necessary, and the variety and cooking that you can do with all the food in the game having no purpose except for what you choose to create (stims and health packs heal much better than food).
There are a few more additions and removals from the game, but essentially what I have described are changes that have fixed the symptoms but not the problem that this game faces. After completing my missions I was right back to the same endgame that I experienced prior to the big overhaul, with nothing to do and very little variety to find. As before, my main goal was to build a Coruscant-like planet, but had to abandon it when the game's framerate went down to a crawl (don't really want to fault the game for that although it was just for my homeworld). Basically, the game still doesn't have a sense of direction or identity that it wants to be. It started out as open-world but have become quite linear with the missions that were added. It has a lot of items and enemy variety aesthetically but practically there are only a few different types of enemies and items. Mining and exploring are still a chore, with too much time staring at your character drilling into the ground for anything large-scale you would like to do. And it is still early access; this has been a very long time with very little progress throughout. Although they have done a fair amount of overhauling in the recent update(s) it has now started to slow back to what it was, which is troubling.
Although it is a great game and I do feel I got my money's worth, I still cannot recommend the game. There is just too troubling looking at the developer's progress and the lack of direction with this game. Although it can be a great distraction and is a good game, it is hard not to see the promise and potential that this game once had.

okay, yes, it had a terrible launch. okay, fine, it took a couple painful months for the patches to roll in. but do you see any other games with its innovation and setting? neither do i. Unity is a vibrant, massive, engaging open world game that is as fun singleplayer as it is running with 3 friends. wether you are just running around slicing up some guards or planning every move in a 20 step heist to get the top score, this game is fun. the armor and weapon selection is crazily in depth, almost like Dark Souls or an MMO. the differences in fighting styles lets you customize how you want to play. i personally favor the spears, sporting a very nice polish blade with a name i cant spell or pronounce. the coloring options, along with the armor, create a personalized experience that really makes you feel connected to your character. upgrading your armor and weapons feels almost like Borderlands, checking stats and trying out a new weapon before you commit to it. the story (im about 3/4s through) is engaging and well voiced and paced. buggy launch and patch issues (which are fixed) aside, i give this game a 8.5/10. its no Skyrim or Super Smash Bros 64, but its way up there. one of the better games ive played in a while.

Osmos to me feels more like a digital zen garden rather than a game. You are what appears to be a sentient soap bubble and you must collide with and absorb all the bubbles smaller than you to grow. There are some unique conditions such as antimatter, bubbles that run away from you, and other AI controlled bubbles to compete against. In order to navigate you must click a direction from which to launch a tiny piece of yourself. This will propel you in the opposite direction and gives a very interesting trade-off between mobility and growth. The game definitely gets tricky fast and I feel like some of the later levels put you at the mercy of the RNG gods, however there is still this overwhelming peacefulness about the whole presentation. While I think people who are easily frustrated will quit playing Osmos rather quickly, if you get into the right mindset, it’s a very relaxing and enjoyable game.

Hacknet is by far the best game that i have ever played, i'll tell you why.
To describe it the most simple it is a text based adventure however in reality it is much more then that.
The story starts of rather cliche with a "if you are reading this i am already dead" though the writer of said story has got a lot more planned.
The basic premise behind Hacknet is as the name suggests "Hacking" though its not your typical CSI mash the buttons fast enough to blow up the CIA sort of hacking. If you aren't familiar with it most hacking is done by exe's and lines of code not a test for how fast you can type the word flamingo.
Most of the commands in hacknet are actually based of UNIX a type of coding language and common PC ports such as SMPT, which is for mail as an example.
The game revolves around the story of you, the player, getting hold of some software known as "Hacknet" basically a UI (User-interface) to easily conduct all your hacking adventures. This program also has a powerful tool known as "porthack" that can be used to eventually break into someone else's computer, this program is quite important later in the story. In the beggining of the game you are greeted by "Bit" or at least his messages that he has left behind. Through an E-Mail system, that is primarly used for attaining new missions, he explains some basics to you.
The thing in Hacknet you are going to spend the most time doing is hacking, this is one by using commands to launch programs that will open up ports on a computer, then once they are all open you can use the aformentioned "Porthack" to finnaly break into the computer, After wich you have to erase your activity of being there so that someone cannot find out if you were there. As the game progresses these sequences become harder for example: adding timers, that when run out will shut down your virtual hacknet computer. a firewall that you have to "analyze" to unlock its password in order to use the "porthack" program. and a proxy that you have to disable with programs run on computer you have already hacked, if this proxy is active you cannot use any of the commands needed for opening up ports.
As the story progresses you find new and interesting ports which you may not have a solution to at first but you will find clever tricks to get around problems you cannot solve by hacking related servers, scanning them for phones and pulling e-mail data out of those to figure out how to solve whatever "puzzle" is stopping you from progressing. Often the characters in the game will give sublte hints via the e-mail system in updates they give after you have completed certain tasks that they asked you to do.
for a text based game it has probably the most tense ending that i have played out of all games ever which really made me realize how good it was.
The characters you meet feel real and "exploration" is very rewarding and can often get you programs or other secret questlines you might have never uncovered otherwise.
I have played this game about 6 times now and i still cannot get enough of it, even now with an added feature to create your complete own storyline inside the game just continues to amaze me.
The only problem i have with it is that at very certain moments the Tab key that auto completes names and commands doesnt completely work and you have to type out and remember a few long words but that's mostly fine. Personally i dont know anything about programming at all yet i was really able to enjoy this game.
For its not massive price tag this is an excellent game that i urge anyone that has a keyboard to play, all in all excellent story and a great atmosphere. a solid 9.5

Pretty dubious. Visibly laggy despite the fact that it looks like it was made in Klik 'n' Play, the main thing that stuck with me was the muted, churchy soundtrack being almost completely drowned out by the huff and puff of constant, equally muted laser and explosion sound effects. There are no sound options to remedy this.
Gameplay consists of wiggling around and holding down the fire key in a pretty fair approximation of a classic shooter, but there's no polish on this game and despite some decent level design in places, the rough edges drag it down.
Keyboard controls don't work properly and a gamepad is required for diagonal movement, which you'll need to get past some of the tougher enemies. Failure is met with a sharp cut to a static, emotionless GAME OVER screen that looks like a screencap of a Playstation 2 game. And, as mentioned, there's the soundtrack: continual and never interesting, it sounds like a beginner going through scales on a pipe organ while someone with a headset microphone records it from the other side of the room.
On the whole, there may be something for you here if you love the genre and don't mind supporting what is clearly a hobbyist game, but if you're looking for something actual, steer clear.

1. I am a spike lee fan and A.A. (That's African American to you) but even I hate that if you aren't black or from Harlem this my career makes no sense. Your family is pre picked,
your nick name is pre picked, the high school and college games feel lifeless and feel unnecessary since they don't impact where you go or where you're drafted. Who says I want to have to play high school and college ball anyway? Just let me get to the NBA. The new story/career mode is also frustrating.  From the very beginning you are given the impression (more than once), that this is an experience that you will build, the kind of thing we've come to expect from a game that allows you to create a player for yourself.  However, by the end of a very short story mode, it is obvious that Spike Lee had a very particular story in mind to tell.  This initial portion of the career mode ends up feeling more like a roadblock you have to get past before you can get to YOUR story.  They also make a terrible decision to restrict your college game time to two 6 minute halves (there is nothing you can do to change this).  There is also a huge disconnect when you listen to a story about a character who is supposedly making millions upon millions of dollars and has his own shoe deal, yet you're still a struggling rookie who's not getting more than a few minutes playtime a game.
Why didn't they stretch out all of the story lines out over a full career instead of forcing me to watch a concentration of cutscenes I didn't care about into 1 year? Which by the way the rookie year is only 8 games so you lose out on an entire season of building up your player. Never have another Spike Lee Joint. More customization.
The announcing sounds like they are reading scripts this year and the post game show leaves me mashing the buttons to get out of it so that I can get to the next game. Too much stuff added as presentation just feels like bloat.
Yes, this year they have added some player interviews into the games, which dazzle a bit with crisp, life-like features.  However, it just comes off with a degree of inconsistantcy when compared with the models you'll see during play-time.  Having said that, overall this is a good looking game whose problems are much more about gameplay and a confusing start to an otherwise interesting career mode.
One of my biggest hopes for this year's game was an improved AI and teammate grading system. Unfortunately, no such luck.  Players still clumsily run out of bounds for no apparent reason, refuse to pass when you are wide open (or respond so late that is results in a missed opportunity), and hold onto the ball for ungodly amounts of time (until they finally pass it to you, forcing you into a bad shot to beat the clock).  Speaking of holding the ball too long, don't make the same mistake yourself.  In addition to the already frustrating actions of the teammate grading system (I just LOVE being penalized for a defensive breakdown, after the game switches my defensive responsibility a half second before the player puts up a wide open shot), if you try to hold onto the ball long enough for someone to get open or to back someone down in the post, your grade is penalized significantly.
To end with full disclosure, I have still been playing this game quite a bit over the last week.  Once you get past the career "story", this year's game has a great new way of handling MyCareer, with new "off-time" choices that can earn you some truly great rewards.

I don't know where to start.
This game is fantastic. It offers so much and the reward for playing this is just pure satisfaction. It is incredibly calming; a great stress reliever, and often you can find yourself lost in the world of Stardew Valley. There are many different parts and systems to the game that I am about to go into more detail about, but beforehand, I must say, buy this game.
Setting/Design:
The location of this game is on a small farm in Stardew Valley. You start out by choosing a type of farm; riverside, forest, etcetera. You start with a basic house and basic tools, and thus begins your journey. The houses, shops, rivers, mines, buildings and interiors are all very well designed and feel incredibly cosy. The foliage such as rocks, trees and grass all look fantastic and add to the environment. Each little detail all adds up to create this indescribable beauty. The pixel graphics provide a more retro feel while also making the game feel cosier and nicer.
Music:
The soundtrack of this game is beautiful. The music is incredibly calming and adds to the feeling that the game gives. Each song has clearly been composed to fit the setting and the scene, and it always adds another dimension to the game, no matter the time.
Sound:
The sounds of this game are surprisingly nice. While not a major part of the game, certain sounds such as trees being cut, water running, fishing, animal noises, crop destruction and even things like the sound of doors and walking are all strangely satisfying and I find I really appreciate this, even though it is so minute.
Character design:
Before starting a new save, you can customise your character, their favourite thing, gender, etcetera. There is an enormous variety of designs, shirts, colours, hair, etcetera, and it makes your character feel unique. It can be fun to mess around with the 'favourite thing' as it comes into the game later on and can make for quite a laugh. You also choose between a cat and a dog, and this will result in a nice surprise later in the game.
Farming:
Obviously, one of the main selling points of this game is the farming, and it does not let you down. This game allows you to farm all sorts of crops and animals. When a season passes, crops die out and you are able to purchase new seeds for a new season. Each crop has a different value, food satisfaction level, type and there are various types of crops. The animal range is also very nice and the element of friendship between your character and the animal also feels really nice and makes the game feel even better.
Friendships:
While this game is a farming game, it also follows a story and the story of the many characters in the town. There are various characters, with a select few that are available to be love interests. Developing friendships with this characters is done in a few ways, and overtime your 'hearts' with each character will increase if you work on the friendship. Some perks of this include the friends giving you items or gifts. There are also various cutscenes when a friendship level increases, and once a certain level is reached, depending on the character, it is possible to marry them and have them move into your house. This makes the game feel more realistic and adds a really warming feel to the overall game.
Progression:
This game is great, however there are some faults. It takes a long time to progress, and this can sometimes be very tedious and make you feel you are doing the same thing over and over. The reward is worth it in the end but it can be quite deterring.
Misc:
There are many different things that can be found in the game or worked towards and unlock new areas around the town, which can provide resources or places to build/farm. This is really nice and the whole concept of refurbishing the community centre is a really nice one.
Conclusion:
This game is great. The soundtrack, the graphics, the systems, etcetera, are all fantastic. I recommend this game to anyone who wants to try something new or wants to enjoy a more retro-ish game, or someone who simply wants to chill out a little from the stresses of life. Whatever your reason, this game is definitely worth picking up.

First of all, this game isn't anything close to the MOBA's people are used to - and I am for one glad for it because I hate them all.
Anyhow, so far it's a great game and I doubt it'll change. P2W is non-existant, there are skins to purchase but as far as it goes, that's the only difference between free and paying user (and they could use a lot more work, since most skins aren't really that "wow" or unique :p )
Players are very cool, and the competition spirit so far is great, probably because game isn't made for everyone and there aren't people yelling stuff you see in usual MOBA's - altho I wouldn't even categorise this game as a MOBA since only similarity with it is the 5v5 type of games, everything else is completely different and unique in comparation.
Each ship is unique in it's own way, and all are useful and good. Even the starter ships can do wonders if you use them well, but if you don't like them, you can test any other ship in firing range and see what floats your boat. :P and purchase it in matter of few games.
Each ship has a lot of things to bring to the table, and that uniqueness is great, some hit real hard but need to be timed and used properly, some hit fast but less damage etc (this is just basic thing, there's a lot more to it than that), so pretty much there's something for everyone.
Gameplay is very fun (except the fact that ships are a bit slow, but well, got used to it real fast)
Gameplay is based on being a tactician and using your cooldowns at the right time, so if you have more people to play with, you can do wonders, altho even "pugs" do very well, but communication is limited to writing - and it's a damn shame there's no VOIP.
A lot of the tactics are based on positioning because if you take too much heat at say front part of the ship, it'll blow your front armour off and you'll be eating a lot more damage than you should've by default, and there's also  general teamplay, you can't win it alone or get fed and just wreck everyone you see, it doesn't work like that.
So far I only played conquest mode, it's basically very similar to Onslaught in Unreal Tournament - basically you fight for nodes to unlock paths to enemy base in order to be able to warp to it and destroy/take it. Also there's a huge fight on the middle of the map every 5(?) minutes when it gets capturable for a huge bonuses (damage, defense, cooldowns etc), so there are some really good fights going on there when everyone warps in there.
Ships got some awesome and crazy looking designs, which I mostly love, but there are few that are damn hilarious, yet they're all cool in their own way.
Graphics and sound are amazing, ship detail is great and weapon, warping and explosion effects really do the job well.
I like this game, and would recommend to anyone who's looking for something a bit different and fun, and something that also requires nice amount of learning curve and a huge amount of teamplay!

First off, i am really convinced that this game deserves more attention as it gets now.
I was beta testing the other capital combat game some months ago that is still in closed beta and compared to Fractured Space, it is just worse.
I really like the graphics in this game, i am an old old eve online player, so the ships are just fitting my personal criteria to be beautiful, impressive and also majestic.
More importantly, the game itself is finished, it feels already complete and is not a half a##ed early access thrown onto steam. At first glance, it seems that it does not offer much in terms of diversity or in regards to maps. But when did the most addictive moba out there (yes it is you LoL) needed different maps?
The mechanics of a game are super important, if it does not feel good, i am the first one to criticize and leave the game, but Fractured Space has a good feel of handling, of moving around and also the combat itself. I had games with a ping of 150 and it felt alright in terms of hit detection, i usually played mechwarrior online, so compared to that, the hit mechanics are far better.
The map design is just perfectly thought through (for conquest), it offers lanes and so many different kinds of tactics you could theoretically use, it is amazing. Even in public games, without super great communication most of the times it feels tactically what you do and not (like in other mobas) frustrating. Of course there are some cases when it is frustrating to see one player do exactly the opposite of what he is supposed to, BUT i have already seen that even this worked out in the end and lost games were won.
I really love it when you notice that a game's gamemode is thought through and just plays out "right".
I am a huge freak for balancing (hello starcraft, mechwarrior) and that is why the other capital ship combat game disappointed me to stop playing. Not with fractured space! Every ship has its purpose, role and unique style of play. Some are easy to learn and yet hard to master, and some are hard to learn but then feel natural very fast.
Never have i experienced that in a game that young and of what i read, the adjustments of balance are only tidbits and not as in other games swinging nerfbats and boosting things to get a sale going.
In terms of pay to win: i have played 4 days long and done 6-10 matches each day and earned me about 500k credits along with some other lootz, so i was able to afford some ships already. But as you start with a neat and good selection anyways this is no problem. The most expensive is not the best. And even if you buy the whole Armada set, this is 31 ships, so you basically pay 1 euro for each ship, imagine that in other mobas ... . This game deserves some cash thrown in, but yet i was hesitant, as i know myself when i buy all 31 ships, i will not really focus on learning a few to be very efficient, so i start slowly.
Just one thing that struck me as i was noticing it, which actually happened a couple times and amazed me: Ship selection is fixed and after the teams select those, you see the enemies choice and can readjust your loadouts.
This is a huge factor in not having team compositions that are just "lame" or "imba" because even if you field too many of one kind, your loadout can be adjusted to deal with the enemy comps better.
Oh, did i mention the SOUNDS? They are awesome, just fkn awesome.
If you like spaceships, flying them and shooting other spaceships, you have no excuse to not download the 8 gig required and just test it (The tutorial does not even feel like a tutorial) for free. What could possibly go wrong? (Okay, you may get as addicted as me hah)

I cannot speak for those who have not played the Dark Souls franchise.
IF YOU HAVE PLAYED DARK SOULS OR BLOODBORNE, KEEP READING.
For anyone who has played a Soulsborne game and enjoyed it, Lords of the Fallen in a perfect representation of what happens when someone other than From tries to make a Souls game. Combat is very clunky, very slow, character stats are very meaningless past a certain point, so there are no individual builds, and ROLLING. Oh my god. The I-frames of the dodge are timed with the very end of the dodge, not the middle. So in order to dodge successfully, and progress through the game (poise does not work), you have to dodge *before* the enemy attacks. Only for hardcore gamers. Or stubborn people like me.

A non-biased quick look @ the game:
It might be short, but its challenging and for the price of a burger or beer it's worth a try. Tiamat X is an old-school style shumup. The evil Choazid Empire has launched a surprise attack on your homeworld, establishing a heavily fortified base from where their forward assault group burrows deep underground, capturing subterranean lifeforms and transforming them into vicious biomechs.
With it being only a matter of time before the Choazids start converting your people, it's up to you to take the controls of one of the few remaining Tiamat dragonship prototypes: the X class fighter, a craft capable of immense firepower - provided you pick up enough upgrade caches during a mission where you must dodge and blast like there's no tomorrow.
Featuring six levels of intense shooting action, Tiamat X is a rip-snortin tribute to the side-scrolling shooters of yesteryear, and would be right at home blazing away on the screen of a booming, beer-stained arcade cabinet. As such, your PC will have to do, and it is much to the designer's regret that he can't plumb a coin-slot into his rig for that truly authentic seaside amusement-park experience.

Everytime you kill an enemy the game pauses/shakes the screen.  This is fine when there are a few enemies, but when there are lots the game becomes a stutterfest and it's almost impossible to control your ship/avoid hitting stuff.
Whether a controller works or not seems random - restarting sometimes fixes it.  A controller is advisable here - being able to sneak or dash is key to completing missions - so it's a pain having to restart the game a few times to make it work.
Some achievements seem reluctant to unlock - most are REALLY hard so it's even more demoralising when they fail to trigger.
As I said earlier, it's a fun concept but it needs a BIT of polishing/some bugfixes and - well - doesn't seem like the developer plans to do any

Fall in line for fast, furious fire fights with Worms Blast. Your mission: launch your worm marine into hostile waters and blast your way to survival through intense puzzle action! Take the big chunk of puzzle-styled gameplay and slice into 60 fun-sized missions. Sprinkle with a fiendishly challenging puzzle mode, and mix in a tasty tournament mode, not forgetting to include the unlockable hidden features. Spread this mixture over a multi-player head-to-head game guaranteeing fun for yourself and your friends, and allow to simmer! When enjoyment is boiling, add in a generous helping of entertaining characters, boat-based silliness, fog, sea monsters, and falling anvils. Add bazookas, dynamite and unprecedented destruction to taste. This recipe should serve a truly hefty helping of fun!
If you like bubble bobble AKA bust a move, tetris attack, or worms, you'll be pleasantly surprised that such a nuanced culmination can exist. I can think of no way in which this game is not perfect. I've been playing this game competitively for years, and with each passing year, new bold strategies to best my opponent keep manifesting. Even the bugs are masterful! Shields don't always work, and you can submerge yourself with a tongue-in-cheek shot offscreen and pop up like a cork on your opponent's terf. If you value your time, play this game with a friend. For the price of a pizza, you can enjoy gaming nirvana.

At it's current state, I don't recommend this game, not even if you get it from a gray key site. No, not becuase "This game is racist because my family is always black and BLAH BLAH BLAH" (those people need help if the really feel like that's racism). I don't recommend it because of what really matter: the gameplay.
Now the game has made some improvements over last year, like some animations are better, it's not as easy to make shots as it was in the last game, slightly better player customization, the rival of MyCrew via the new ProAm mode (even if we can't play on our courts yet), MyCourt, some bugs/glitches fixed, etc. However there's a lot of new issues in the game, incuding some from the old game. For example, Demigods and hackers are back on MyPark. People have had 99 overalls since the day came out for people who preordered and managed to get things outside of their rank (skateboards, shirtless option, mascot gear, etc). Speaking of MyPark, the servers are very hit or miss. Either it runs smoothly or everyone lags the entire time and the game runs like a slideshow. Also there's an issue with the Got Next spots that sometimes happens that prevents anyone from getting on them. Also, that 1v1v1 mode they have in MyPark is kinda lame, but that's just me nitpicking.
Moving onto MyCareer, it's also kind of a mess. The story is lame. I understand them wanting you to feel like a high school/college phenom, nad those games were fun, but once you get drafted is where I have issues with it. You're being being drafted amongst player that have ratings in the upper 70s (probably some in the lower 80s as well) but your overall is at a 55 to start, and yet the characters in the story talk about you potentially going lottery pick in the draft. The rookie season is only 8 games, which isn't that bad, except you basically get no VC at that point so you don't rank up that much going into your 2nd season. Also they advertised the new MyCareer story to make you think it's all about choices, but you really don't until you finish the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t story. The only choice you get is the college you go to, and even then you only get about 10(?) choices for schools. Once your rookie season is over is when you actually get to make choices, which I enjoy. I like that you get to choose how you spend your off days, even though I wish you'd get more VC out of endorsements (since it doesn't seem like you make that much in games, regardless of how wellyou do).
The biggest issue I have with the game, however, is the stability. Whenever I do MyCareer or Play Now games, my frames drop a lot, the game stutters, and the game crashes a lot. The game sometimes switches from full screen to windowed mode for no reason no matter what my settings are. All in all, I'd say just wait for a patch before you buy the game.

First of all, this game isn't anything close to the MOBA's people are used to - and I am for one glad for it because I hate them all.
Anyhow, so far it's a great game and I doubt it'll change. P2W is non-existant, there are skins to purchase but as far as it goes, that's the only difference between free and paying user (and they could use a lot more work, since most skins aren't really that "wow" or unique :p )
Players are very cool, and the competition spirit so far is great, probably because game isn't made for everyone and there aren't people yelling stuff you see in usual MOBA's - altho I wouldn't even categorise this game as a MOBA since only similarity with it is the 5v5 type of games, everything else is completely different and unique in comparation.
Each ship is unique in it's own way, and all are useful and good. Even the starter ships can do wonders if you use them well, but if you don't like them, you can test any other ship in firing range and see what floats your boat. :P and purchase it in matter of few games.
Each ship has a lot of things to bring to the table, and that uniqueness is great, some hit real hard but need to be timed and used properly, some hit fast but less damage etc (this is just basic thing, there's a lot more to it than that), so pretty much there's something for everyone.
Gameplay is very fun (except the fact that ships are a bit slow, but well, got used to it real fast)
Gameplay is based on being a tactician and using your cooldowns at the right time, so if you have more people to play with, you can do wonders, altho even "pugs" do very well, but communication is limited to writing - and it's a damn shame there's no VOIP.
A lot of the tactics are based on positioning because if you take too much heat at say front part of the ship, it'll blow your front armour off and you'll be eating a lot more damage than you should've by default, and there's also  general teamplay, you can't win it alone or get fed and just wreck everyone you see, it doesn't work like that.
So far I only played conquest mode, it's basically very similar to Onslaught in Unreal Tournament - basically you fight for nodes to unlock paths to enemy base in order to be able to warp to it and destroy/take it. Also there's a huge fight on the middle of the map every 5(?) minutes when it gets capturable for a huge bonuses (damage, defense, cooldowns etc), so there are some really good fights going on there when everyone warps in there.
Ships got some awesome and crazy looking designs, which I mostly love, but there are few that are damn hilarious, yet they're all cool in their own way.
Graphics and sound are amazing, ship detail is great and weapon, warping and explosion effects really do the job well.
I like this game, and would recommend to anyone who's looking for something a bit different and fun, and something that also requires nice amount of learning curve and a huge amount of teamplay!

This is a great game for those who want a difficult, well polished, and streamlined rougelike RPG. It is the kind of game where, even if you prepare to the fullest, you can still taste the bitter sting of defeat. As they say though, luck favors the prepared. Some players do not like games where they can fail despite all their best effort, or just see a hero mercilessly struck down, never to be able to be used again. However, some of the situations this game puts you in have have led to some truly great moments.
The atmosphere and artwork are remarkably consistent, and the UI is intuitive and well made. Many of the reviews I have seen simply take for granted how amazing it is to have a clean, responsive user interface. Its something you don't realize or think about until you try to play a game with a clunky interface. Just know, if you had to deal with the stress of a bad interface in addition to the stress of your party, the stress on the player would make this game almost unplayable. Thankfully, this is not the case.

First off, i am really convinced that this game deserves more attention as it gets now.
I was beta testing the other capital combat game some months ago that is still in closed beta and compared to Fractured Space, it is just worse.
I really like the graphics in this game, i am an old old eve online player, so the ships are just fitting my personal criteria to be beautiful, impressive and also majestic.
More importantly, the game itself is finished, it feels already complete and is not a half a##ed early access thrown onto steam. At first glance, it seems that it does not offer much in terms of diversity or in regards to maps. But when did the most addictive moba out there (yes it is you LoL) needed different maps?
The mechanics of a game are super important, if it does not feel good, i am the first one to criticize and leave the game, but Fractured Space has a good feel of handling, of moving around and also the combat itself. I had games with a ping of 150 and it felt alright in terms of hit detection, i usually played mechwarrior online, so compared to that, the hit mechanics are far better.
The map design is just perfectly thought through (for conquest), it offers lanes and so many different kinds of tactics you could theoretically use, it is amazing. Even in public games, without super great communication most of the times it feels tactically what you do and not (like in other mobas) frustrating. Of course there are some cases when it is frustrating to see one player do exactly the opposite of what he is supposed to, BUT i have already seen that even this worked out in the end and lost games were won.
I really love it when you notice that a game's gamemode is thought through and just plays out "right".
I am a huge freak for balancing (hello starcraft, mechwarrior) and that is why the other capital ship combat game disappointed me to stop playing. Not with fractured space! Every ship has its purpose, role and unique style of play. Some are easy to learn and yet hard to master, and some are hard to learn but then feel natural very fast.
Never have i experienced that in a game that young and of what i read, the adjustments of balance are only tidbits and not as in other games swinging nerfbats and boosting things to get a sale going.
In terms of pay to win: i have played 4 days long and done 6-10 matches each day and earned me about 500k credits along with some other lootz, so i was able to afford some ships already. But as you start with a neat and good selection anyways this is no problem. The most expensive is not the best. And even if you buy the whole Armada set, this is 31 ships, so you basically pay 1 euro for each ship, imagine that in other mobas ... . This game deserves some cash thrown in, but yet i was hesitant, as i know myself when i buy all 31 ships, i will not really focus on learning a few to be very efficient, so i start slowly.
Just one thing that struck me as i was noticing it, which actually happened a couple times and amazed me: Ship selection is fixed and after the teams select those, you see the enemies choice and can readjust your loadouts.
This is a huge factor in not having team compositions that are just "lame" or "imba" because even if you field too many of one kind, your loadout can be adjusted to deal with the enemy comps better.
Oh, did i mention the SOUNDS? They are awesome, just fkn awesome.
If you like spaceships, flying them and shooting other spaceships, you have no excuse to not download the 8 gig required and just test it (The tutorial does not even feel like a tutorial) for free. What could possibly go wrong? (Okay, you may get as addicted as me hah)

I"ve decided to update my review and change my recommendation, with caveats...
.....I thought this would be a fun, relaxed sort of puzzle game. The mechanics are simple. The environment and music are pleasant.
.....If you play the Ambient levels, it is exactly that. A fun enjoyable experience that moves at a comfortable pace. Puzzles range from easy to moderately hard but not frustrating.
.....The Sentient levels however are a different story.
.....In the Sentient levels you are competing against AI organisms that are very difficult to overcome. You have to Alt-Z a LOT to get a freshly generated map, in the hopes that you will get a starting point that gives you some chance of winning. And even then winning may depend heavily on luck. Expect to restart a LOT.
.....The Force levels are frustrating but not as much as the Sentient levels. With more time I think I can find my peace with them. But thus far I have not been willing to invest the effort. After all, this was supposed to be a game that would allow me to relax and just have a bit of fun.
.....So, if you want what the game advertises; a  relaxing ethereal sort of distraction with some challenging puzzle aspects, Play and Enjoy the Ambient levels and the beginner levels of the other two trees.
.....If you are looking for a more difficult challenge that retains the basic playability of the ambient levels, try the more advanced Force levels.
.....If you are a sadist, enjoy beating your head against a wall, and relying largely on luck to win, go for the upper Sentient levels.
.....In the end, my recommendation comes down to whether or not I would buy the game again. Considering the price (I paid like $3.99 for it) I would say yes. It is an enjoyable game IF you stick to the modes you like. But I would not have paid full price for it.
